definition_en: to pull your eyebrows together, showing displeasure or deep thought
core_image: 老师皱着眉低头看作业本
scene: 老师看着乱糟糟的作业本，皱起了眉头。 The teacher frowned at the messy exercise book.
sceneCN: 这里 frown 是「皱眉」（第 1 个义项）；句意：老师看着乱糟糟的作业本，皱起了眉头。

senses.title: Pull the brows together
senses.definition: to move your eyebrows together because you are angry, worried, or thinking hard
senses.definitionCN: 因生气、担忧或苦苦思索而把眉毛皱在一起
senses.example: The teacher frowned at the messy exercise book.
senses.exampleCN: 老师看着乱糟糟的作业本，皱起了眉头。
senses.why: This is the basic facial action the word names.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词所指的基本面部动作。

senses.title: Show disapproval
senses.definition: to disapprove of something, often used with on or upon
senses.definitionCN: 不赞成某事，常与 on 或 upon 连用
senses.example: Many parents frown on late-night phone use.
senses.exampleCN: 许多家长不赞成深夜玩手机。
senses.why: A frown signals that something is not acceptable.
senses.whyCN: 皱眉表示某事不被接受。

senses.title: The frown itself
senses.definition: an expression in which the brows are pulled tightly together
senses.definitionCN: 双眉紧锁的表情
senses.example: A deep frown crossed his face.
senses.exampleCN: 他脸上掠过一道深深的皱眉。
senses.why: The action can also be named as a thing.
senses.whyCN: 这个动作也可以作为一个名词来称呼。

intro.en: Frown came into English from Old French.
intro.cn: frown 从古法语进入英语。

items.en: Froignier meant to wrinkle the nose or scowl.
items.cn: froignier 意为皱起鼻子或做出苦相。

items.en: The word appeared as frounen.
items.cn: 这个词以 frounen 的形式出现。

items.en: The spelling became frown.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 frown。

items.en: The sense widened to any look of displeasure.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何不悦的神情。

items.en: Frown on became a common phrase for disapproval.
items.cn: frown on 成为表示不赞成的常用短语。

note.en: Frown is compared with look-alike words and words for facial expressions.
note.cn: 把 frown 与形近词以及表示面部表情的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: A frown is the face that says something is wrong.
normalIntro.cn: 皱眉是那张表示出了问题的人脸。

normal.en: The teacher frowned at the messy exercise book.
normal.cn: 老师看着乱糟糟的作业本皱起了眉。

normal.en: Many parents frown on late-night phone use.
normal.cn: 许多家长不赞成深夜玩手机。

normal.en: A deep frown crossed his face.
normal.cn: 他脸上掠过一道深深的皱眉。

normal.en: She frowned in confusion at the strange map.
normal.cn: 她对着那张奇怪的地图困惑地皱眉。

normal.en: He answered with a frown and a short sigh.
normal.cn: 他皱着眉、短叹一声作答。

abstract.en: A frown is a question the mouth cannot ask.
abstract.cn: 皱眉是嘴巴问不出的问题。

abstract.en: Not every frown is anger; some are deep thought.
abstract.cn: 并非每次皱眉都是生气，有些是深思。

abstract.en: One lowered brow can say more than a long speech.
abstract.cn: 一低眉有时胜过长篇大论。

examples.en: The teacher frowned at the messy exercise book.
examples.cn: 老师看着乱糟糟的作业本皱起了眉头。

examples.en: Many parents frown on late-night phone use.
examples.cn: 许多家长不赞成深夜玩手机。

dict_mnemonic.text: frown 与 brown、drown 形近，注意区分首字母；frown on 表示「不赞成」，不要直译成「在……上皱眉」。

root: 源自古法语 froignier（皱鼻、做苦相），可能与日耳曼语有关；核心义「眉头收紧」。

sensesIntro.en: Frown names the facial action, the disapproval it shows, and the expression itself.
sensesIntro.cn: frown 指皱眉的动作、它所表达的不赞成，以及皱眉的表情。

core.en: Brows pulled together to show feeling.
core.cn: 双眉收紧以表达情绪。

branches.en: The brows meet above worried eyes.
branches.cn: 双眉在忧虑的双眼上方相聚。

branches.en: The look warns that something is not accepted.
branches.cn: 这种神情警告某事不被接受。

branches.en: The tightened face becomes a visible object.
branches.cn: 紧绷的脸变成可见的表情。

branches.en: Thought and disapproval share the same muscles.
branches.cn: 思索与不赞成共用同样的肌肉。

branches.en: A parent's frown teaches without a word.
branches.cn: 父母的皱眉不用言语就能教导。

intro.en: Frown builds a small family of words about the lowered brow.
intro.cn: frown 构成一小族与皱眉有关的词。

latinIntro.en: Frown comes from Old French, not from Latin.
latinIntro.cn: frown 来自古法语，并非拉丁语。

items.example: Do not frown at your little brother.
She frowns whenever she reads small print.
He frowned and closed the book.
She stood frowning at the screen.

items.meaning: to direct a frown toward someone
items.example: The guard frowned at the noisy crowd.
items.exampleCN: 警卫对着吵闹的人群皱眉。

items.example: A deep frown showed his doubt.
items.exampleCN: 深深的皱眉显出他的怀疑。

definition_en: very good at doing something, showing careful control
core_image: 巧手把碎瓷片严丝合缝地拼回去
scene: 她用灵巧的双手把碎瓷片拼回原样。 With skillful hands she pieced the broken china back together.
sceneCN: 这里 skillful 是「灵巧的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她用灵巧的双手把碎瓷片拼回原样。

senses.title: Full of skill
senses.definition: very good at doing something with your hands or mind
senses.definitionCN: 用手或脑做好某事的能力很强
senses.example: With skillful hands she pieced the broken china back together.
senses.exampleCN: 她用灵巧的双手把碎瓷片拼回原样。
senses.why: This is the main sense of practiced ability.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示熟练能力的主要义项。

senses.title: Showing fine craft
senses.definition: showing great care and ability in making something
senses.definitionCN: 在制作某物时表现出极大的细心与能力
senses.example: The box shows skillful work.
senses.exampleCN: 这个盒子显示出精湛的工艺。
senses.why: Work itself can carry the quality of skill.
senses.whyCN: 作品本身也能体现技艺的质量。

senses.title: Good at a task
senses.definition: good at handling a particular kind of task
senses.definitionCN: 善于处理某类特定任务
senses.example: She is skillful at settling arguments.
senses.exampleCN: 她善于调解争执。
senses.why: The pattern skillful at names a strength.
senses.whyCN: skillful at 这一搭配用来指出长处。

intro.en: Skillful joins the noun skill with -ful.
intro.cn: skillful 由名词 skill 加 -ful 构成。

items.en: Skil meant understanding or judgment.
items.cn: skil 意为理解或判断。

items.en: The suffix -full meant full of.
items.cn: 后缀 -full 意为充满……的。

items.en: Skill entered English as a noun.
items.cn: skill 作为名词进入英语。

items.en: Skill and -ful combined as skillful.
items.cn: skill 与 -ful 组合成 skillful。

items.en: It now praises hands, work, and judgment.
items.cn: 如今它用来赞美双手、作品和判断力。

note.en: Skillful is compared with look-alike words and words for ability.
note.cn: 把 skillful 与形近词以及表示能力的词作比较。

entries.definition: doing what one wants anyway
causing pain
paying attention to avoid harm
having trained ability
very good at something
quick and neat with the hands

normalIntro.en: Skillful means full of skill, in hands and in work.
normalIntro.cn: skillful 意为双手和作品里都充满技巧。

normal.en: With skillful hands she pieced the broken china back together.
normal.cn: 她用灵巧的双手把碎瓷片拼回原样。

normal.en: The box shows skillful work.
normal.cn: 这个盒子显示出精湛的工艺。

normal.en: She is skillful at settling arguments.
normal.cn: 她善于调解争执。

normal.en: The skillful driver avoided every hole.
normal.cn: 熟练的司机避开了每个坑。

normal.en: He made a skillful cut in the wood.
normal.cn: 他在木头上做了精准的切割。

abstract.en: Skillful hands make difficulty look simple.
abstract.cn: 灵巧的双手让困难看起来简单。

abstract.en: Care in small things becomes skill in large ones.
abstract.cn: 对小事的细心会变成对大事的熟练。

abstract.en: Skillful work leaves no loud marks of effort.
abstract.cn: 精湛的作品不会留下用力的喧哗痕迹。

examples.en: With skillful hands she pieced the broken china back together.
examples.cn: 她用灵巧的双手把碎瓷片拼回原样。

examples.en: The box shows skillful work.
examples.cn: 这个盒子显示出精湛的工艺。

examples.en: She is skillful at settling arguments.
examples.cn: 她善于调解争执。

dict_mnemonic.text: skillful = skill（技能）+ -ful（充满）；skillfully 是副词，skillfulness 是名词。

root: 由 skill（技能）加后缀 -ful（充满……的）构成；核心义「充满技艺的」。

sensesIntro.en: Skillful describes able hands, fine work, or ease at handling a task.
sensesIntro.cn: skillful 形容灵巧的双手、精湛的作品，或处理任务时的娴熟。

core.en: Hands and mind working with easy control.
core.cn: 双手与头脑从容掌控地工作。

branches.en: Fingers place each piece exactly.
branches.cn: 手指把每一片放得恰到好处。

branches.en: The finished object shows quiet care.
branches.cn: 完成的作品显示出安静的用心。

branches.en: Words settle a quarrel without noise.
branches.cn: 言语无声地平息争执。

branches.en: The maker and the made thing share one quality.
branches.cn: 制作者与作品共享同一种品质。

branches.en: Skill can guide people, not only tools.
branches.cn: 技艺不仅能驾驭工具，也能引导人。

intro.en: Skillful describes the quality produced by skill.
intro.cn: skillful 描述由技能产生的品质。

latinIntro.en: The root is Germanic; only the suffix is English.
latinIntro.cn: 词根属日耳曼语；后缀属英语。

items.exampleCN: 她是一位技术娴熟的外科医生。
她的灵巧让评委印象深刻。

items.example: An unskillful cut ruined the cloth.
items.exampleCN: 不熟练的一刀毁了布料。
灵巧的双手修好了玩具。
这件雕刻是精湛的工艺。

definition_zh: 使合并；使成为一体；融入
definition_en: to combine two or more things so that they work together as one whole
core_image: 几块零散的零件被装进同一台机器，接线合成一个回路
scene: 车间里摆着几个各自能转的旧装置，工程师把它们接到同一个控制盘上。 The new software lets us integrate billing and delivery into one screen.
sceneCN: 这里 integrate 是「使合并为一体」（第 1 个义项：把几部分结合成整体），句意为新软件让我们把账单和配送合到同一屏幕。画面里的物件：旧装置、控制盘、接线。

pos.zh: 动词：使合并；使一体化；融入

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ion 构成，义为「整合；一体化」
由过去分词转作形容词，义为「综合的；一体化的」
由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「有整合作用的」
由否定前缀 dis- 加本词构成，义为「瓦解；分解」

senses.title: Join parts into a whole
senses.definition: to combine separate parts or systems so that they form one working whole
senses.definitionCN: 把彼此分开的部分或系统组合成一个能运转的整体
senses.example: The team spent a year integrating the two computer systems.
senses.exampleCN: 团队花了一年时间把两套电脑系统整合起来。
senses.why: Latin integer means untouched and whole; integrare is to make whole again.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 integer 意为「完整无损」，integrare 即「使之重新完整」。

senses.title: Fit into a new group
senses.definition: to become an accepted part of a group, school, or society
senses.definitionCN: 成为某个群体、学校或社会中被接受的一员
senses.example: New students need time to integrate into the class.
senses.exampleCN: 新生需要时间融入班级。
senses.why: The social sense grew in the twentieth century, when schools and workplaces stopped separating groups.
senses.whyCN: 社会义在二十世纪成长起来，那时学校与工作场所不再分隔不同群体。

senses.title: Do the combining
senses.definition: to arrange for two activities or services to be handled together
senses.definitionCN: 安排两项活动或服务一并处理
senses.example: The hotel integrated its booking system with the airline's.
senses.exampleCN: 这家酒店把预订系统与航空公司的连在一起。
senses.why: Businesses picked up the word because customers want one bill, not three.
senses.whyCN: 商业界采纳这个词，因为顾客想要一张账单而不是三张。

intro.en: Integrate rests on the Latin adjective integer "whole", a favourite word of Roman writers on number and health.
intro.cn: integrate 基于拉丁语形容词 integer「完整的」，这是罗马作家谈数目与健康时爱用的词。

items.en: Integer means whole, untouched, in good condition, from in- "not" and a root for touching.
items.cn: integer 意为「完整的、未被触动的、状况良好的」，由 in-「不」与表示「触碰」的词根构成。

items.en: Integrare "to make whole, to renew" appears in classical prose.
items.cn: integrare「使完整、更新」见于古典散文。

items.en: Integratio "a renewing" was used for restoring a whole state, including health.
items.cn: integratio「更新」用于恢复完整状态，也包括健康。

items.en: English took the verb in the seventeenth century for rebuilding a whole from parts.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪借入这个动词，指用部分重建整体。

items.en: The twentieth century added the social sense of groups learning to live together.
items.cn: 二十世纪又添上了群体学会共处的社会义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the Latin root for wholeness; the near-meaning group holds other words for joining.
note.cn: 形近组共享拉丁语「完整」词根；近义组收其他表示「结合」的词。

entries.definition: A whole number, one undivided unit.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「整数」，即不可分割的整单位。

entries.definition: Wholeness of character; an unbroken state.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「正直；完整」，指品行或状态的完整无损。

entries.definition: Necessary to the whole, not optional.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「构成整体所必需的」。

entries.definition: To put things together, often while keeping them distinct.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「结合」，各成分往往仍可分辨。

entries.definition: To join so that the parts lose their separate lines.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「合并」，各部分界线消失。

entries.definition: To bring people or groups together for one aim.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「联合」，多用于人与团体为一目标而合。

normalIntro.en: The hooks build on integer, the whole number at the heart of the word.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子建立在词中间的 integer「整数」之上，那正是「完整」的意思。

normal.en: integer is a whole number: integrate is to make a whole.
normal.cn: integer 是完整的数：integrate 就是把东西做成完整。

normal.en: Integrate the two systems with one cable, and the bill appears once.
normal.cn: 用一根线把两套系统整合，账单就只出现一次。

normal.en: Immigrants integrate into a town by working, voting, and making friends.
normal.cn: 移民靠工作、投票和交朋友融入一座城镇。

normal.en: Dis- plus integrate gives the very opposite: to fall apart.
normal.cn: dis- 加 integrate 恰好是其反面：瓦解。

normal.en: A good designer integrates form and purpose.
normal.cn: 好的设计师把形式与用途合成一体。

abstract.en: To integrate is to let many voices become one choir.
abstract.cn: 整合就是让许多声音变成一个合唱。

abstract.en: A whole is not the pile of parts but the fit between them.
abstract.cn: 整体不是零件的堆叠，而是它们之间的契合。

abstract.en: Integration happens when a newcomer stops being a guest.
abstract.cn: 当新人不再是客人，融合就发生了。

examples.en: We must integrate the new staff into the team quickly.
examples.cn: 我们必须让新员工迅速融入团队。

examples.en: The app integrates maps with live train times.
examples.cn: 这款应用把地图与实时列车时刻结合起来。

examples.en: It takes years to integrate these small farms into one market.
examples.cn: 要把这些小农场并入同一个市场需要多年时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因太鬼特的」——零件太奇特，也得整合成一台机器

root: 拉丁语 tangere「触碰」→ in-「不」+ tangere → integer「未被触动的、完整的」→ integrare「使完整」→ 英语 integrate。同族词：integrity、integral、disintegrate。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: combining systems, fitting into a group, and linking services for convenience.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：整合系统、融入群体，以及为便利把服务连在一起。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose parts wired into one working machine.
core.cn: 核心意象：零散零件被接线成一台能运转的机器。

branches.en: THE CONTROL PANEL: separate devices answer to one board.
branches.cn: 控制盘这条线：分开的装置听命于同一块面板。

branches.en: THE CLASSROOM: a newcomer becomes part of the group.
branches.cn: 教室这条线：新来的人成为群体的一部分。

branches.en: THE SINGLE BILL: two services are handled as one.
branches.cn: 一张账单这条线：两项服务被并作一件处理。

branches.en: THE LINK: both senses remove the seams between things.
branches.cn: 连接线：两个义项都在消除事物之间的接缝。

branches.en: THE LINK: parts and people both become whole by fitting in.
branches.cn: 连接线：零件与人都是靠嵌合才变得完整。

intro.en: Integrate splits into in- "not", the root teg- "touch", and the verb ending -ate.
intro.cn: integrate 可拆为 in-「不」、词根 teg-「触碰」与动词词尾 -ate。

latinIntro.en: Latin integer, integrare and integratio are all recorded forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 integer、integrare、integratio 都是有记载的形式。

items.example: It gives the sense of untouched.
items.exampleCN: 它给出「未被触动」的意思。

items.example: The root also appears in contact and intact.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根也见于 contact 与 intact。

items.example: The adjective also gives English integer.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词也给出英语的 integer。

items.example: It is the direct source of the verb.
items.exampleCN: 它是这个动词的直接来源。

items.example: It marks a verb of action.
items.exampleCN: 它标出表示动作的动词。

items.example: The noun keeps the whole idea.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词保留了「完整」的意念。

items.example: The prefix turns wholeness into collapse.
items.exampleCN: 前缀把完整变成了崩解。

definition_en: a farm or place where milk is produced, a shop selling milk, or products made from milk
core_image: 清晨，奶牛排队走进挤奶棚，桶里冒着热气
scene: 清晨，奶牛排队走进挤奶棚，桶里冒着热气。 The dairy sends fresh milk to the town each morning.
sceneCN: 这里 dairy 指「奶牛场」（第 1 个义项：生产牛奶的地方）；句意是这个奶牛场每天早上把鲜奶送到镇上。

senses.title: A milk farm
senses.definition: a farm or building where milk is produced and kept
senses.definitionCN: 生产并存放牛奶的农场或房屋
senses.example: The dairy sends fresh milk to the town each morning.
senses.exampleCN: 这个奶牛场每天早上把鲜奶送到镇上。
senses.why: Milk must be collected in one place before it can travel.
senses.whyCN: 奶总要先在一个地方聚起来，才能往外送。

senses.title: A milk shop
senses.definition: a shop that sells milk, butter, and cheese
senses.definitionCN: 出售牛奶、黄油和奶酪的店铺
senses.example: He bought butter at the dairy.
senses.exampleCN: 他在乳品店买了黄油。
senses.why: Before fridges, milk had to be sold the same day it came.
senses.whyCN: 在没有冰箱的年代，奶得当天就卖掉。

senses.title: Made from milk
senses.definition: relating to milk or made from it, used before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 与奶有关或用奶制成，用在名词前
senses.example: The dairy counter was full of cheese.
senses.exampleCN: 乳品柜台摆满了奶酪。
senses.why: A place word can turn into a label for what it sells.
senses.whyCN: 一个地方的名字，能变成它卖的东西的标签。

intro.en: Dairy comes from Old English dæge, a woman servant, whose duties grew to include milking and making milk products.
intro.cn: dairy 源自古英语 dæge（女仆），她的活计逐渐包含挤奶和做奶制品。

items.en: Dæge named a woman servant in a household.
items.cn: dæge 指家里的女仆。

items.en: Her work came to include milking the cows.
items.cn: 她的活儿后来包括给奶牛挤奶。

items.en: Dey became the place where milk was worked.
items.cn: dey 变成处理牛奶的地方。

items.en: Dairy named both the room and the farm for milk.
items.cn: dairy 既指做奶的屋子，也指产奶的农场。

items.en: Dairy now also covers milk products and their industry.
items.cn: dairy 如今还涵盖乳制品及其行业。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the dai- shape, and the meaning group names milk and the places that handle it.
note.cn: 形近组共享 dai- 外形，近义组列出牛奶与处理牛奶的场所。

entries.definition: happening every day
a book for daily notes
a small white flower with a yellow centre
a place where milk is turned into butter
entries.definitionCN: 把牛奶做成黄油的场所

entries.definition: the white liquid produced by cows
the act of taking milk from an animal
entries.definitionCN: 从动物身上取奶的动作

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with cows walking into a shed and end with a counter full of cheese.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从奶牛走进棚子开始，落到摆满奶酪的柜台。

normal.en: Dairy began as a woman's job and ended as a whole industry.
normal.cn: dairy 从一个女人的活计开始，最后成了一整个行业。

normal.en: Milk cannot wait, so the dairy must be near the cow.
normal.cn: 奶等不起，所以奶牛场得离牛很近。

normal.en: Dairy and diary differ by one letter and by a whole day.
normal.cn: dairy 和 diary 只差一个字母，也差着一整天的记录。

normal.en: A dairy counter is a farm seen through glass.
normal.cn: 乳品柜台，就是隔着玻璃看到的一座农场。

normal.en: If it comes from a cow and is white, it may be dairy.
normal.cn: 如果它来自奶牛又是白色的，那可能就是乳制品。

abstract.en: Picture a row of cows waiting at a low door.
abstract.cn: 想象一排奶牛在一道矮门前等着。

abstract.en: Picture a steel can of milk breathing steam.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钢桶里的牛奶冒着热气。

abstract.en: Picture a glass case of yellow butter blocks.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃柜里一块块黄色的黄油。

examples.en: The dairy sends fresh milk to the town each morning.
examples.cn: 这个奶牛场每天早上把鲜奶送到镇上。

examples.en: He bought butter at the dairy.
examples.cn: 他在乳品店买了黄油。

examples.en: The dairy counter was full of cheese.
examples.cn: 乳品柜台摆满了奶酪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 dairy 记成「奶棚」：天一亮奶牛进棚，挤出的奶就在这个 dairy 里变成黄油和奶酪。

root: 源自古英语 dæge（女仆），她原先管揉面，后来也管挤奶与做奶制品；地方名 dey 逐渐演变为 dairy，指产奶、存奶与卖奶的场所。

sensesIntro.en: From the farm that produces milk, to the shop that sells it, to the label on the products themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 从产奶的农场，到卖奶的店铺，再到奶制品本身的标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: cows filing into a shed where milk is collected.
core.cn: 核心意象：奶牛排队走进收集牛奶的棚子。

branches.en: The first place is the farm or shed where milk is kept.
branches.cn: 最初的场所，是存放牛奶的农场或棚屋。

branches.en: The same word names the shop that sells the milk.
branches.cn: 同一个词也指卖奶的店铺。

branches.en: As a label it marks butter, cheese, and cream.
branches.cn: 作为标签，它标出黄油、奶酪和奶油。

branches.en: The farm and the shop are two ends of one route.
branches.cn: 农场和店铺，是同一条路的两端。

branches.en: A shop and its goods can share a single name.
branches.cn: 店铺和它的货物，可以共用一个名字。

intro.en: Dairy has a small English family, all of it tied to milk and to the work of producing it.
intro.cn: dairy 的英语词族不大，全都和牛奶以及产奶的活计有关。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root; it comes from Old English dæge, a woman servant.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，它来自古英语 dæge（女仆）。

definition_zh: 低声说；耳语；悄悄说；沙沙作响
definition_en: to speak very quietly, using breath rather than voice, so that only a person close by can hear
core_image: 一个人凑到另一个人耳边，用手挡着嘴，只放出一点气声
scene: 图书馆里，有人俯身凑到同伴耳边，用手挡着嘴，只放出一点气声。 She leaned over and whispered the answer in my ear.
sceneCN: 这里 whisper 是「低声说、耳语」（第 1 个义项：只用气声而不振动声带地说话）；句意为她探过身来，在我耳边小声说出答案。凑到耳边、用手挡嘴、只放出一点气声的动作就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: To speak with breath
senses.definition: to say something in a very quiet voice, without vibration of the vocal cords
senses.definitionCN: 用极轻的声音说话，声带不振动
senses.example: She leaned over and whispered the answer in my ear.
senses.exampleCN: 她探过身来，在我耳边小声说出答案。
senses.why: The word imitates the sound itself: a hissing movement of breath without voice.
senses.whyCN: 这个词摹拟的就是声音本身：一股只有气、没有嗓音的嘶嘶气流。

senses.title: To sound softly
senses.titleCN: 沙沙作响；发出轻柔的响声
senses.definition: to make a soft continuous sound like a quiet stream or moving leaves
senses.definitionCN: 发出像细流或树叶摇动那样的轻柔连续声响
senses.example: The leaves whispered as the wind moved through them.
senses.exampleCN: 风穿过树叶，树叶沙沙作响。
senses.why: Anything that sounds like breath without a voice can be said to whisper, so the word moved from people to nature.
senses.whyCN: 凡听起来像无嗓音气息的东西都能说是在低语，于是这个词从人扩展到了自然。

senses.title: To talk in secrets
senses.definition: used of people passing information quietly, often news that is not yet public
senses.definitionCN: 指人们悄悄地传递消息，常常是尚未公开的新闻
senses.example: People whisper that the company is about to be sold.
senses.exampleCN: 人们私下议论说这家公司即将被出售。
senses.why: Quiet words travel only between close ears, so telling a secret and whispering became the same act.
senses.whyCN: 轻细的话只在近处的耳朵之间传递，于是说秘密和低语成了同一个动作。

senses.title: The quiet sound itself
senses.definition: as a noun, the quiet sound of speech without voice or of a soft rustle
senses.definitionCN: 作名词时指不带嗓音的轻声话语，或轻微的沙沙声
senses.example: They spoke in a whisper so the baby would not wake.
senses.exampleCN: 他们低声说话，免得吵醒孩子。
senses.why: The noun simply turns the act into a thing, and it also names the sound of a stream.
senses.whyCN: 名词只是把动作变成事物，同时也用来称溪流的声音。

intro.en: Whisper is a Middle English word of imitative origin, first written whispren, and its form has hardly changed since.
intro.cn: whisper 是中古英语的摹声词，最早写作 whispren，此后词形几乎没有变化。

items.en: Old English had hwisprian for murmuring, built from a base that already imitated a hiss.
items.cn: 古英语已有 hwisprian（喃喃低语），其词根本身就摹拟嘶嘶声。

items.en: The verb appeared as whispren and whisperen, and the noun followed close behind.
items.cn: 动词写作 whispren、whisperen，名词紧随其后出现。

items.en: The word gained its secret-telling sense, and to whisper news came to mean to spread a rumour.
items.cn: 这个词获得了「悄悄传话」的意思，whisper news 便指散布传言。

items.en: Nature writers used it for the sound of leaves and streams, widening the picture.
items.cn: 自然文学作家用它形容树叶与溪流的声音，扩大了这幅画面。

items.en: The noun stays in fixed phrases such as in a whisper and a whisper of doubt.
items.cn: 名词义保留在 in a whisper 与 a whisper of doubt 这类固定短语里。

note.en: The first group gathers words of the same quiet shape, the second the ways of speaking at low volume.
note.cn: 第一组收字形相近的同族安静词，第二组收低声说话的各种说法。

entries.definition: A thin curl of smoke or hair.
The shrill sound made through the lips.
A stiff hair on an animal's face.
The quiet sound taken as a noun.
A low continuous sound with voice in it.
To speak unclearly, with mouth nearly shut.
The sharp breath sound of s.

normalIntro.en: The word is built out of the sound it names: a hiss of air with no voice behind it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是用它所命名的声音拼出来的：一股没有嗓音的气流嘶嘶作响。

normal.en: Say it very quietly and the word performs itself.
normal.cn: 轻声把这个词念出来，它就在演示自己。

normal.en: The whis at the start is the same hiss as in whistle.
normal.cn: 开头的 whis 与 whistle 里的嘶声相同。

normal.en: No voice, only air: that is the difference from speaking quietly.
normal.cn: 只有气没有嗓音：这就是它与小声说话的区别。

normal.en: Leaves, streams and rumours all whisper.
normal.cn: 树叶、溪流和传言都会 whisper。

normal.en: In a whisper keeps the noun, while whisper to keeps the verb.
normal.cn: in a whisper 留住名词义，whisper to 留住动词义。

abstract.en: Feel warm breath at the edge of an ear.
abstract.cn: 感受耳畔一股温热的气。

abstract.en: See a hand cupped beside a mouth.
abstract.cn: 想一只手挡在嘴边。

abstract.en: Hear a room where nobody raises a voice.
abstract.cn: 听一个谁都不提高嗓子的房间。

examples.en: Do not whisper in class; ask me after the lesson.
examples.cn: 上课别小声说话，下课来问我。

examples.en: He whispered a few words and she nodded.
examples.cn: 他小声说了几句，她点了点头。

examples.en: A whisper ran through the crowd before the result was read.
examples.cn: 结果宣读之前，人群里传开了一阵低语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威斯珀」——威斯珀凑到耳边只吹气不出声。

root: 古英语 hwisprian（喃喃低语，摹声词）→ 中古英语 whisperen → 现代英语 whisper。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as voice-less breath, then lends that sound to leaves and streams, then to secrets passed between close ears, and finally stands as a noun for the soft sound itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从无嗓音的气流开始，把这声音借给树叶与溪流，再借给近耳之间传递的秘密，最后作为名词指那轻柔的声音本身。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: breath released beside an ear.
core.cn: 核心意象：在耳边放出的一口气。

branches.en: The quiet speech branch: the answer whispered in my ear.
branches.cn: 轻声说话分支：在我耳边说出的答案。

branches.en: The nature branch: leaves whispering in the wind.
branches.cn: 自然分支：风中的树叶沙沙作响。

branches.en: The rumour branch: people whisper that the firm will be sold.
branches.cn: 传言分支：人们私下议论公司将被出售。

branches.en: The noun branch: speaking in a whisper.
branches.cn: 名词分支：低声说话。

branches.en: The idiom branch: a whisper of doubt.
branches.cn: 习语分支：一丝疑虑的低语。

intro.en: Whisper is an imitative whole word; its family is built with -ing, -er and -y rather than with real prefixes.
intro.cn: whisper 是摹声的整体词，它的词族靠 -ing、-er、-y 构成，而不是靠真正的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin used susurrus for a whisper, itself an imitation of the sound; the entries below are counterparts, not ancestors of whisper.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 susurrus 表示低语，它本身也是摹声词；下面的条目是对应形式，并非 whisper 的祖先。

items.example: The hiss is in the letters.
It joins the word to politics.

definition_zh: 估价；评估；赏识；感激；增值；货币升值；鉴赏
definition_en: the act of estimating the quality or worth of something; recognition of value; gratitude; an increase in value; also a written or spoken expression of approval
core_image: 把一件东西放上估价的天平：先称出它值多少，再承认它值钱，最后为这份价值心生感激
scene: 在画廊里，鉴定师在灯下端详一件小铜像，写下估值。 Its appreciation took three experts two days.
sceneCN: 这里 appreciation 是「估价；评估价值」（第 1 个义项：判断某物的品质与价值）；句意：这件小铜像的估价花了三位专家两天时间。

pos.zh: 估价；评估；赏识；感激；增值；鉴赏

collocations.zh: 深切的感激；深刻的理解

derivatives.zh: 未受赏识的；未被感激的

senses.title: Estimating worth: putting a value on something
senses.titleCN: 估定价值：给某物定个价
senses.definition: the act of estimating the quality, condition, or monetary worth of something
senses.definitionCN: 判断某物的品质、状况或金钱价值的行为
senses.example: The appreciation of the painting took three experts two days.
senses.exampleCN: 鉴定这幅画的价值花了三位专家两天时间。
senses.why: Late Latin appretiare is ad- 'to' plus pretium 'price': to set a price on a thing. The first English sense, recorded c.1600, is exactly this act of estimating quality and worth.
senses.whyCN: 晚期拉丁语 appretiare 是 ad-“向”加 pretium“价格”：给某物定个价。英语最早记录于约 1600 年的义项，正是这种判断品质与价值的行为。

senses.title: Recognition of value: esteeming what is good
senses.definition: a favorable estimate of someone or something; the recognition that something is valuable or excellent
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某物的高评价；承认某物有价值或很出色的认识
senses.example: Her appreciation of the old craftsman's skill grew with every visit.
senses.exampleCN: 每去一次，她对这位老匠人技艺的赏识就多一分。
senses.why: If the estimated worth is high, the estimate becomes esteem. After c.1650 appreciation commonly carried this 'high estimate' sense: the scale tips upward and the word names recognition rather than mere measurement.
senses.whyCN: 如果估出的价值很高，估价就变成器重。约 1650 年之后，appreciation 通常带有“高估”之义：天平向上倾斜，词义也从单纯的测量转为“认出价值”。

senses.title: Gratitude: valuing what someone has done
senses.titleCN: 感激：珍视别人所做之事
senses.definition: the feeling of being thankful for a kindness or benefit, and of recognizing its worth
senses.definitionCN: 因受到善意或帮助而心存感谢，并承认这份好处的价值
senses.example: He wrote a short note of appreciation to the nurse who stayed late.
senses.exampleCN: 他给那位守到很晚的护士写了一张简短的感谢便条。
senses.why: The thing now valued is another person's act. To appreciate a kindness is to put a high worth on it, and that estimate surfaces as gratitude — the emotional form of 'it was worth a lot to me'.
senses.whyCN: 此时被估价的是他人的行为。appreciate 一份善意，就是给它很高的价值，而这份估价浮上来就成感激——也就是“这对我很值”的情感形式。

senses.title: Rise in value: the asset gains worth
senses.definition: an increase in the value of property, shares, or other assets over time
senses.definitionCN: 房产、股票或其他资产随时间而增加的价值
senses.example: The house's appreciation paid for their daughter's tuition.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋房子的增值支付了他们女儿的学费。
senses.why: The noun shifts from the act of valuing to the value itself moving upward. The 1784 sense 'a rise in value' is the price side of pretium growing, not a new estimate being made.
senses.whyCN: 名词从“估价的动作”转到“价值本身向上走”。1784 年出现的“价值上升”义，是 pretium 的“价格”一面在增长，而不是又做了一次估价。

senses.title: A formal valuation: the official figure
senses.titleCN: 正式估价：官方核定的数字
senses.definition: a formal assessment of value, as for tax, insurance, or sale, often recorded as a figure
senses.definitionCN: 为税务、保险或出售而做的正式价值评估，通常落成一个数字
senses.example: The insurance appreciation came in well below the rebuild cost.
senses.exampleCN: 保险估价远低于重建成本。
senses.why: The 1799 sense 'act of setting a value on' narrows the first sense into an official act. Here the estimate is written down and binding, so appreciation becomes a valuation document rather than a private judgment.
senses.whyCN: 1799 年出现的“给某物定价的行为”把最早义项收窄为一种官方行为。此时估价被写下来并具有约束力，appreciation 也就从私人判断变成一份估价文件。

senses.title: An expression of approval: the words of praise
senses.titleCN: 赞赏之辞：说出来的好评
senses.definition: a spoken or written statement that recognizes the good qualities of someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 口头或书面承认某人某物优点的表述
senses.example: The review was a warm appreciation of the young pianist.
senses.exampleCN: 那篇评论是对这位年轻钢琴家的热情赞赏。
senses.why: The 1858 sense 'expression of favorable estimation' externalizes the inner estimate. What was a judgment in the mind becomes words; the noun now names the tribute rather than the appraisal.
senses.whyCN: 1858 年出现的“表达有利评价”把内心的估价外化。原本在心里的判断变成了话语；名词此时命名的是称许，而不是评估过程。

senses.title: Understanding the significance: seeing why it matters
senses.titleCN: 体认意义：明白它为何重要
senses.definition: a clear understanding of the importance, difficulty, or meaning of something
senses.definitionCN: 对某事的重要性、难度或意义的清楚理解
senses.example: Living through the drought gave them a new appreciation of water.
senses.exampleCN: 经历过那场干旱，他们对水有了新的体会。
senses.why: To value something fully you must see what it costs or what it does. This branch moves from worth to understanding: the estimate is now a grasp of significance, as in an appreciation of the difficulty.
senses.whyCN: 要真正看重某物，必须看见它的代价或作用。这条分支从“价值”转到“理解”：估价在这里变成对意义的把握，如 appreciation of the difficulty（对困难的认识）。

senses.title: Currency appreciation: the money grows stronger
senses.titleCN: 货币升值：钱变得更值钱
senses.definition: an increase in the exchange value of a currency relative to other currencies
senses.definitionCN: 一种货币相对于其他货币的汇兑价值上升
senses.example: A sharp appreciation of the yen made imports cheaper.
senses.exampleCN: 日元的急剧升值让进口商品变便宜了。
senses.why: This is the asset sense applied to a whole currency: its price in other currencies rises. The word still measures worth, but the worth being measured is the money itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是资产义应用到整种货币上：它以其他货币计的价格上升。这个词仍在衡量价值，只是被衡量的对象变成了钱本身。

senses.title: Aesthetic appreciation: taste trained on art
senses.titleCN: 审美鉴赏：被艺术训练过的眼光
senses.definition: the trained enjoyment and evaluation of art, music, or beauty, based on discernment rather than mere liking
senses.definitionCN: 对艺术、音乐或美的有训练的欣赏与评价，基于鉴别力而非单纯喜欢
senses.example: The course teaches the appreciation of Renaissance painting.
senses.exampleCN: 这门课教授文艺复兴绘画的鉴赏。
senses.why: The recognition sense is applied to beauty: the viewer estimates quality, feels its worth, and is pleased. Aesthetic appreciation is thus valuation and gratitude-like delight fused into taste.
senses.whyCN: “认出价值”的义项被用到美上：观者判断品质，感到它可贵，并因此愉悦。审美鉴赏于是是估价与类似感激的喜悦融合成趣味。

intro.en: Appreciation entered English c.1600 from French appréciation, the action noun of apprécier, and behind both stands Late Latin appretiare 'estimate the quality of' — ad- 'to' plus pretium 'price'. The suffix -ion turns the act into a noun. Its family is the price family, not the proper family of appropriate and not the near family of approximate.
intro.cn: appreciation 约于 1600 年从法语 appréciation 进入英语，它是 apprécier 的动作名词；两者背后是晚期拉丁语 appretiare“评估品质”——ad-“向”加 pretium“价格”。后缀 -ion 把这个动作变成名词。它属于“价格”词族，既不是 appropriate 的“自己的”词族，也不是 approximate 的“最近”词族。

items.en: First recorded as 'act of estimating the quality and worth of something'. The earliest sense is valuation, not gratitude.
items.cn: 最早记录为“判断某物品质与价值的行为”。最早的义项是估价，而不是感激。

items.en: From French appréciation, the action noun of apprécier (14c.). French passed on both the noun and the verb pattern, with -tion marking an action or its result.
items.cn: 来自法语 appréciation，即 apprécier（14 世纪）的动作名词。法语把名词和动词模式一并传下，-tion 标记动作或其结果。

items.en: Appretiare 'estimate the quality of' = ad- 'to' + pretium 'price'. The verb literally sets a price on a thing, so worth and price are one idea at the root.
items.cn: appretiare“评估品质”= ad-“向”+ pretium“价格”。这个动词字面上就是给某物定价，因此在词根处，价值与价格是同一个概念。

items.en: After c.1650 the noun generally includes a 'high estimate'; 1784 adds 'a rise in value', and 1799 'act of setting a value on'. Esteem, market gain and official valuation split off from the first sense.
items.cn: 约 1650 年之后，这个词通常含有“高估”；1784 年增加“价值上升”义，1799 年增加“给某物定值的行为”义。器重、市场增值与官方估价从最早义项中分了出来。

items.en: Appreciate is recorded only in the 1650s, later than appreciation. The 1858 sense 'expression of favorable estimation' adds spoken or written praise.
items.cn: appreciate 直到 17 世纪 50 年代才有记录，晚于 appreciation。1858 年出现的“表达有利评价”义，增加了口头或书面的称许。

items.en: All senses still run through pretium 'price': estimate a price, value it highly, feel its worth, watch it rise. Appropriate (proprius 'one's own') and approximate (proximus 'nearest') are different roots that only look alike.
items.cn: 所有义项仍贯穿 pretium“价格”：估一个价、把价估高、感到它可贵、看着它上涨。appropriate（proprius“自己的”）与 approximate（proximus“最近的”）只是形近，词根完全不同。

note.en: The first group separates appreciation from two famous look-alikes that belong to different roots; the second group separates it from words of gratitude and valuation that share only part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组把 appreciation 与两个著名的形近词分开，它们属于不同词根；第二组把它与只共享部分含义的“感激”和“估价”词分开。

entries.definition: to value, understand, be grateful for, or rise in value. It shares the pretium root, but it is recorded in the 1650s, later than appreciation c.1600.
entries.definitionCN: 重视；理解；感激；增值。它与 appreciation 共享 pretium 词根，但直到 17 世纪 50 年代才有记录，晚于约 1600 年的 appreciation。

entries.definition: suitable or proper for a purpose. It comes from proprius 'one's own', not from pretium 'price', so it is not a relative of appreciation.
entries.definitionCN: 合适的；恰当的。它来自 proprius“自己的”，而不是 pretium“价格”，因此不是 appreciation 的同族词。

entries.definition: close to the correct value but not exact. It comes from proximus 'nearest', a third root that merely looks similar.
entries.definitionCN: 接近正确值但不精确的。它来自 proximus“最近的”，是第三个只是看起来相似的词根。

entries.definition: the feeling of being thankful. It covers only the emotional branch, while appreciation also means valuation and increase in value.
entries.definitionCN: 感激之情。它只覆盖情感分支，而 appreciation 还表示估价与增值。

entries.definition: the act of publicly acknowledging someone's merit or existence. It stresses acknowledgment, while appreciation stresses the high value placed on the thing.
entries.definitionCN: 公开承认某人的功绩或存在。它强调“承认”，而 appreciation 强调给某物很高的评价。

entries.definition: an expert or official estimate of monetary value. It is the technical valuation branch, while appreciation can also mean esteem or gratitude.
entries.definitionCN: 专家或官方对金钱价值的估算。它是技术性的估价分支，而 appreciation 还可以指器重或感激。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: pretium 'price', the documented dates c.1600 / 1650s / 1784 / 1799 / 1858, and the fixed phrases express appreciation and capital appreciation.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：pretium“价格”，有据可查的年代 1600／17 世纪 50 年代／1784／1799／1858，以及 express appreciation、capital appreciation 等固定搭配。

normal.en: Pretium is 'price'. Appreciation begins as putting a price on a thing, which is why the word can mean valuation before it means gratitude.
normal.cn: pretium 是“价格”。appreciation 的起点是给某物定价，所以它会先表示估价，之后才表示感激。

normal.en: Appreciation is recorded c.1600 but appreciate only in the 1650s: the noun came first, and the verb followed.
normal.cn: appreciation 约记录于 1600 年，而 appreciate 到 17 世纪 50 年代才出现：名词先来，动词后到。

normal.en: Capital appreciation is the rise of an asset's price; currency appreciation is the rise of a currency against others.
normal.cn: capital appreciation 是资产价格上涨；currency appreciation 是一种货币对其他货币的升值。

normal.en: Express appreciation is the standard phrase for saying thank you in a formal setting.
normal.cn: express appreciation 是在正式场合表达感谢的标准说法。

normal.en: An appreciation of art is trained taste: the same word that prices a bronze bird also judges a painting.
normal.cn: an appreciation of art 是受过训练的趣味：给铜鸟估价的同一个词，也用来品评一幅画。

abstract.en: A balance with a small object on one pan and weights on the other: the needle settles, and the object now has a worth.
abstract.cn: 一架天平，一盘放小物件，一盘放砝码：指针停住，这件东西便有了价值。

abstract.en: The needle can move up two ways: someone raises the estimate, or the object itself becomes more valuable. Appreciation covers both.
abstract.cn: 指针可以向上走两种方式：有人提高估价，或物件本身变得更值钱。appreciation 两者都覆盖。

abstract.en: Once worth is felt as a personal gift, the scale turns into a thank-you note: valuation and gratitude are the same estimate seen from inside.
abstract.cn: 当价值被感受为一份私人馈赠，天平就变成一张感谢便条：估价与感激是同一个判断的内外两面。

examples.en: The audience showed its appreciation with a long round of applause.
examples.cn: 观众以长久的掌声表达赞赏。

examples.en: Land in the district has seen steady appreciation over ten years.
examples.cn: 这个区的土地十年来稳步增值。

examples.en: Travel gave her a deeper appreciation of how differently people live.
examples.cn: 旅行让她更深刻地体会到人们的生活方式有多么不同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿普瑞希爱申」——阿普（Ap）把画举到灯下估价，瑞希（Rui Xi）看得连连点头，爱申（Ai Shen）写下“很值钱” → appreciation 欣赏、感激、增值

root: 源自晚期拉丁语 appretiare“estimate the quality of”（ad-“向”+ pretium“价格”），核心是给事物定价、估出价值，再由“估得高”引申为赏识、感激与增值。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of appreciation all start from a pair of scales: something is priced, the price is judged high, the high worth is felt as gratitude, and the value itself may rise. Art, formal documents and currencies are later fields for the same estimate.
sensesIntro.cn: appreciation 的九个义项都从一架天平开始：给某物定价，判断价格很高，把这份高价值感受为感激，而价值本身还可能上涨。艺术、正式文件与货币只是这同一估价行为后来进入的领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an object placed on a scale and given a worth.
core.cn: 核心意象：把一件东西放上天平，给它一个价值。

branches.en: ESTIMATE AND VALUATION: the original act of judging worth, and its official, written form.
branches.cn: 估价与核价：判断价值的最初行为，以及它官方化、书面化的形式。

branches.en: RECOGNITION AND TASTE: esteeming what is excellent, including the trained appreciation of art.
branches.cn: 赏识与趣味：器重出色之物，包括受过训练的艺术鉴赏。

branches.en: GRATITUDE: the high estimate of a kindness, felt as thankfulness.
branches.cn: 感激：把一份善意估得很高，并在心里感受为感谢。

branches.en: ASSETS AND CURRENCY: worth that rises, whether in property or in money itself.
branches.cn: 资产与货币：价值向上走，无论对象是房产还是货币本身。

branches.en: PRAISE AND UNDERSTANDING: the estimate spoken aloud, and the grasp of why something matters.
branches.cn: 称许与理解：说出口的评价，以及对某物为何重要的把握。

intro.en: Appreciation is appreciat- plus -ion, from Latin -ionem, which names an action or its result. English builds appreciate, appreciative, appreciatively, appreciable, appreciably and unappreciated on the same stem, and de- gives the opposite depreciate.
intro.cn: appreciation 是 appreciat- 加 -ion，后者来自拉丁语 -ionem，命名动作或其结果。英语在同一词干上构造出 appreciate、appreciative、appreciatively、appreciable、appreciably 与 unappreciated，而 de- 给出反方向的 depreciate。

latinIntro.en: The direct source is Late Latin appretiare, ad- plus pretium 'price'. Latin pretium also gives pretiare 'to price' and depretiare 'to lower the value of'; none of these belongs to proprius or proximus.
latinIntro.cn: 直接来源是晚期拉丁语 appretiare，即 ad- 加 pretium“价格”。拉丁语 pretium 还给出 pretiare“定价”与 depretiare“降低价值”；这些都不属于 proprius 或 proximus。

items.structure: appreciat- (set a value) + -ion (action or result noun)
items.meaning: valuation, esteem, gratitude, or increase in value
items.meaningCN: 估价；赏识；感激；增值（-ion 构成动作或结果名词）
items.example: She showed her appreciation with a handwritten card.
items.exampleCN: 她用一张手写卡片表达感谢。

items.meaning: to value, understand, thank, or increase in worth
items.meaningCN: 重视；理解；感激；增值（-ate 构成动词）
items.example: I appreciate your help more than I can say.
items.exampleCN: 我对你的帮助感激不尽。

items.meaning: showing gratitude or sensitive to value
items.meaningCN: 感激的；有鉴赏力的（-ive 构成形容词）
items.example: The audience was appreciative of the small ensemble.
items.exampleCN: 观众对这个小乐团很是欣赏。

items.meaning: in a grateful or admiring way
items.meaningCN: 感激地；赞赏地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She smiled appreciatively at the gift.
items.exampleCN: 她对这份礼物感激地笑了。

items.meaning: large enough to be noticed or measured
items.meaningCN: 可察觉的；相当可观的（-able 构成形容词）
items.example: There was an appreciable drop in temperature.

items.meaningCN: 明显地；可观地（-ly 构成副词）

items.meaning: not recognized or thanked for one's value
items.meaningCN: 未受赏识的；未被感激的（un- 表示否定）
items.exampleCN: 夜班员工觉得自己未受重视。

items.meaning: to fall in value, or to belittle
items.meaningCN: 贬值；贬低（de-“向下”+ preci-“价格”+ -ate）
items.example: The car depreciates as soon as it is driven away.

latinEntries.meaning: to estimate the quality or value of
to lower the value of, disparage

definition_zh: 使成为；给予；提供；翻译；演奏
definition_en: to cause something to be in a certain state, or to give or perform something
core_image: 把手里的东西双手递还给对方
scene: 那场事故让他半年不能走路。 The accident rendered him unable to walk for six months.
sceneCN: 这里 render 是「使成为」（第 1 个义项：使某物陷入某种状态）；句意：那场事故使他半年不能走路。

pos.zh: 使成为；给予；提供；翻译；演奏

derivatives.zh: render 加 -ing 构成，义为「演绎；译文；渲染」
经法语再借入的形式，义为「演绎；表演版本」
加前缀 sur- 构成，义为「交出；投降」，与 render 同源

senses.title: To cause something to be in a state
senses.definition: to make someone or something be in a particular condition
senses.definitionCN: 使某人或某物处于某种特定状况
senses.example: The flood rendered the road impassable.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水使这条路无法通行。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to give back, and giving a new condition to something is a kind of handing over.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「交还」，而给某物一个新的状态，也是一种交付。

senses.title: To give or provide something
senses.definition: to give help, a service, or a decision in a formal way
senses.definitionCN: 以正式方式给予帮助、服务或作出决定
senses.example: The doctor rendered first aid at the scene.
senses.exampleCN: 医生在现场施行了急救。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply giving, which survives in formal phrases about services and verdicts.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的一层就是「给」，这一点在关于服务和裁决的正式说法中保留下来。

senses.title: To express in another language or form
senses.definition: to put a text or an idea into another language or another medium
senses.definitionCN: 把文本或想法转换成另一种语言或媒介
senses.example: The poem is hard to render into English.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗很难译成英语。
senses.why: Giving back the meaning of a text in another tongue is a giving in the same old sense.
senses.whyCN: 用另一种语言把文本的意义交出来，仍是那个古老的「给」。

senses.title: To perform or play something
senses.definition: to perform a piece of music, a role, or an interpretation
senses.definitionCN: 演奏一段音乐、扮演一个角色或作出一种演绎
senses.example: She rendered the song with great tenderness.
senses.exampleCN: 她非常温柔地演绎了这首歌。
senses.why: A performance gives the work back to the audience in the performer's own form.
senses.whyCN: 表演是演奏者用自己的形式把作品交还给观众。

intro.en: Render comes from Old French rendre, from Latin reddere, to give back, built on red- and dare, to give.
intro.cn: render 来自古法语 rendre，源自拉丁语 reddere「交还」，由 red- 与 dare「给」构成。

items.en: Dare means to give, and is also behind data, the things given.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，也是 data（被给出的东西）的词源。

items.en: Reddere adds red- to dare and means to give back or hand over.
items.cn: reddere 在 dare 前加 red-，意为交还或交出。

items.en: Rendre means to give back, to yield, and to translate.
items.cn: 古法语 rendre 表示交还、让与以及翻译。

items.en: English render covers giving, causing a state, and expressing in another form.
items.cn: 英语 render 涵盖给予、使处于某种状态以及以另一种形式表达。

items.en: The word keeps a formal tone in phrases about services, verdicts, and translations.
items.cn: 这个词在涉及服务、裁决与翻译的说法中保持正式语气。

note.en: Render comes from the same Latin giving verb as surrender, and it stands near words for giving and for translation.
note.cn: render 与 surrender 出自同一个拉丁「给」的动词，并与表示给予和翻译的词相邻。

entries.definition: a performance, translation, or version of something
entries.definitionCN: 演绎；译文；版本，由 render 加 -ing 构成

entries.definition: a particular performance of a song or role
entries.definitionCN: 演绎；表演版本，经法语再次借入的形式

entries.definition: to give up or hand over
entries.definitionCN: 交出；投降，与 render 同出拉丁语 reddere

entries.definition: to give something that is needed
entries.definitionCN: 提供；供给，与第二义项接近

entries.definition: to cause something to become
entries.definitionCN: 使成为，与第一义项接近

entries.definition: to express words in another language

normalIntro.en: The Latin base means to give back, so the hooks all picture handing something over.
normalIntro.cn: 拉丁词根意为「交还」，所以记忆钩子都在想象把东西递过去。

normal.en: Red- plus dare, to give, gives give back, which grows into give and make.
normal.cn: red- 加 dare「给」，就是「交还」，再发展为给予与使成为。

normal.en: Surrender is the same verb with a different prefix, so both hand something over.
normal.cn: surrender 是同一个动词换了个前缀，两者都是把东西交出去。

normal.en: Render a service, render a verdict, and render assistance are formal fixed phrases.
normal.cn: render a service、render a verdict、render assistance 都是正式固定说法。

normal.en: The pattern render plus object plus adjective is common: render it useless.
normal.cn: render 加宾语加形容词的句型很常见：render it useless。

normal.en: Rendering and rendition both name a version of a work.
normal.cn: rendering 与 rendition 都指作品的某个版本。

abstract.en: Picture both hands holding an object out to another person.
abstract.cn: 想象双手把一件东西捧到对方面前。

abstract.en: See a translator turning a page of poetry into another language.
abstract.cn: 想象译者把一页诗变成另一种语言。

abstract.en: Think of a pianist giving a piece back to a silent room.
abstract.cn: 想一位钢琴家把一首曲子交还给安静的房间。

examples.en: The storm rendered the bridge unsafe.
examples.cn: 暴风雨使这座桥变得不安全。

examples.en: Volunteers rendered help to the injured.
examples.cn: 志愿者向伤者提供了帮助。

examples.en: The novel has been rendered into twelve languages.
examples.cn: 这部小说已被译成十二种语言。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「软的」——想象把软软的东西双手递过去，这就是「给予」；只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古法语 rendre，源自拉丁语 reddere（red-「回」+ dare「给」），核心为「交还、给出」。

sensesIntro.en: Handing something over grows into giving help, giving a thing a new condition, giving a text a new language, and giving a work a performance.
sensesIntro.cn: 「把东西交出」长成四个方面：给出帮助、给事物一个新状态、给文本一种新语言、给作品一次演绎。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: something held out in both hands.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手把东西递到对方面前。

branches.en: Giving a thing a condition is the most abstract form of handing over.
branches.cn: 给事物一个状态，是「交出」最抽象的形式。

branches.en: Giving help or a verdict is the plainest survival of the old sense.
branches.cn: 给予帮助或作出裁决，是古义最朴素的留存。

branches.en: Giving the meaning in another language is translation.
branches.cn: 用另一种语言把意义交出来，就是翻译。

branches.en: Giving a work back as sound or action is performance.
branches.cn: 把作品以声音或动作交还，就是演绎。

branches.en: Both are acts of formal delivery to another party.
branches.cn: 两者都是向另一方正式交付的行为。

intro.en: Render carries a Latin prefix and the Latin verb for giving, reshaped by French.
intro.cn: render 携带拉丁前缀与表示「给」的拉丁动词，并经过法语改造。

latinIntro.en: Latin red- means back, and dare means to give, so reddere means to give back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁前缀 red- 表示「回」，dare 表示「给」，因此 reddere 意为「交还」。

items.example: Red- marks the returning of what is given.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 red- 标记所给之物的回返。

items.example: The da- root also appears in data.
items.exampleCN: da- 词根也出现在 data 中。

items.example: Dare is the oldest layer of the word.
items.exampleCN: dare 是这个词最古老的一层。

items.example: Rendre ends in -re, which becomes -er in English.
items.exampleCN: rendre 以 -re 结尾，进入英语后写作 -er。

items.example: Reddere is the direct Latin source.
items.exampleCN: reddere 是直接的拉丁来源。

items.meaningCN: 表示行为或结果的名词词尾
items.example: Rendering names a version or an act of rendering.
items.exampleCN: rendering 指某个版本或演绎行为。

items.example: Surrender means to hand over completely.
Data is the plural of the Latin word for given things.
items.exampleCN: data 是拉丁语「被给出之物」的复数。

definition_en: the outside of something; the way something looks from outside; outer
core_image: 一栋房子从街上看过去的外墙与屋顶
scene: 这栋楼的外墙刷成了白色。 The exterior of the building is painted white.
sceneCN: 这里 exterior 是「外部、外面」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这栋楼的外墙刷成了白色。

senses.title: The outside
senses.definition: the outer surface or outside of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物的外表面或外部
senses.example: The exterior of the house needs paint.
senses.exampleCN: 房子的外墙需要刷漆。
senses.why: The core sense is the outer side of a thing.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是事物的外侧。

senses.title: Outward appearance
senses.definition: the way someone or something looks from outside
senses.definitionCN: 人或物从外面看起来的样子
senses.example: Despite his calm exterior, he was worried.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管外表平静，他其实很担心。
senses.why: The outer surface becomes a show of appearance.
senses.whyCN: 外表面变成呈现出来的样子。

senses.title: Outer
senses.definition: on or from the outside
senses.definitionCN: 位于外部或来自外部的
senses.example: The exterior walls are very thick.
senses.exampleCN: 外墙非常厚。
senses.why: The noun becomes an adjective of position.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为表示位置的形容词。

intro.en: Exterior comes from Latin exterior, the comparative of exterus, outward.
intro.cn: exterior 来自拉丁语 exterior，是 exterus（向外的）的比较级。

items.en: Exterus means outward or foreign.
items.cn: exterus 意为向外的或外来的。

items.en: Exterior means more outward.
items.cn: exterior 意为更靠外的。

items.en: The word contrasts with interior.
items.cn: 这个词与 interior 相对。

items.en: Exterior reaches English through French forms.
items.cn: exterior 经法语形式进入英语。

items.en: Exterior names both the outside and its look.
items.cn: 现代英语中 exterior 兼指外部与外观。

note.en: Exterior is the outside; interior is the inside.
note.cn: exterior 是外部，interior 则是内部。

entries.definition: the inside of something
better or higher in rank
lower in quality or rank
the outer part of something
the top or outer layer
pointing or facing away from the inside

normalIntro.en: Exterior is the outside surface and the look it presents.
normalIntro.cn: exterior 指外表面以及它呈现出来的样子。

normal.en: The exterior of the car was dusty.
normal.cn: 汽车的外表布满灰尘。

normal.en: They painted the exterior walls last summer.
normal.cn: 他们去年夏天刷了外墙。

normal.en: His cheerful exterior hid a deep sadness.
normal.cn: 他愉快的外表掩盖着深深的悲伤。

normal.en: The building's exterior is made of stone.
normal.cn: 这栋楼的外墙是石头做的。

normal.en: Exterior lighting makes the path safe at night.
normal.cn: 室外照明让夜间的小路安全。

abstract.en: Picture a house seen from the street at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象黄昏时从街上看到的一栋房子。

abstract.en: Imagine a calm face covering a worried mind.
abstract.cn: 想象一张平静的脸掩盖着担忧的心。

abstract.en: Think of a shell protecting what lies inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一层外壳保护着里面的东西。

examples.en: The exterior of the museum is plain stone.
examples.cn: 博物馆的外墙是朴素的石头。

examples.en: She kept a calm exterior during the interview.
examples.cn: 面试时她保持着平静的外表。

examples.en: Exterior doors must be kept locked.
examples.cn: 外门必须保持上锁。

dict_mnemonic.text: exterior 与 external 同源，都表示「外面的」；exterior 更强调外表与外观。

root: 源自拉丁语 exterior（更靠外的），是 exterus（向外的）的比较级，核心义「外部与外观」。

sensesIntro.en: Exterior means the outside of something, its outward appearance, or outer.
sensesIntro.cn: exterior 意为某物的外部、其外观，或外部的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a house wall facing the street.
core.cn: 核心意象：朝向街道的一面房屋外墙。

branches.en: The base sense is the outside of a thing.
branches.cn: 基础义是事物的外侧。

branches.en: The surface becomes the look presented to others.
branches.cn: 表面变成呈现给他人的样子。

branches.en: The noun becomes an adjective of position.
branches.cn: 名词转为表示位置的形容词。

branches.en: The outside and its appearance are closely linked.
branches.cn: 外部与其外观紧密相连。

branches.en: Outward appearance and outer position both face away from the inside.
branches.cn: 外表与外位都朝向内部之外。

intro.en: Exterior belongs to the Latin exterus family, like external and extreme.
intro.cn: exterior 属于拉丁语 exterus 词族，与 external、extreme 同源。

latinIntro.en: Latin exterus and exterior are the source forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 exterus 与 exterior 是来源形式。

items.example: The book shows the exteriors of old houses.
items.exampleCN: 这本书展示了老房子的外部。

items.example: The idea of exteriority is central here.
items.exampleCN: 外在性的概念在这里很重要。

items.example: The interior is warm and bright.
He externalized his fears in art.
items.exampleCN: 他在艺术中把恐惧外化。

latinEntries.example: Extra is related to the outer family.

definition_zh: 编织；织（布）；编造；（穿行）蜿蜒
definition_en: to cross threads or strips over and under each other to make cloth, and also to move in and out of things
core_image: 梭子从一排绷紧的经线间穿过，把一根横线压进去，布面一点点长出来
scene: 老人坐在门口的木凳上，双手一推一拉，梭子来回穿过线阵，一块粗布慢慢铺开来。 She wove with a steady shuttle, and the cloth grew under her hands.
sceneCN: 这里 weave 是「编织」（第 1 个义项：让线交错而成布）；句意为梭子来回穿行，布在她手下一点点长出来。穿过经线的梭子与逐渐成形的布面就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 编织；织布；编造；蜿蜒穿行

senses.title: To make cloth from threads
senses.definition: to cross threads over and under each other so that cloth or a mat results
senses.definitionCN: 让线彼此上下交错，织成布或席
senses.example: They weave wool into heavy blankets for winter.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把羊毛织成厚毯子过冬。
senses.why: This is the physical core: two sets of threads crossing.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理核心：两组线交叉。

senses.title: To make something by crossing strips
senses.definition: to make an object by passing long strips over and under each other
senses.definitionCN: 把长条相互上下穿接，做成器物
senses.example: He wove thin reeds into a flat basket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把细芦苇编成一只扁篮。
senses.why: The same crossing action works on reeds and wire as on yarn.
senses.whyCN: 同样的交错动作，用于芦苇与铁丝，也用于纱线。

senses.title: To move in and out
senses.definition: to move along a winding path, passing between other things
senses.definitionCN: 沿弯曲路径移动，从其他事物之间穿过
senses.example: The road weaves between the hills.
senses.exampleCN: 这条路在山丘之间蜿蜒穿行。
senses.why: A shuttle goes in and out of the warp, and a path may do the same.
senses.whyCN: 梭子在经线间进出，路径也可以这样走。

senses.title: To invent a story
senses.definition: to put details together into a story or an account
senses.definitionCN: 把细节拼合成故事或叙述
senses.example: She wove three old tales into one novel.
senses.exampleCN: 她把三个旧故事编进了一部小说。
senses.why: Strands joined into cloth give the image for details joined into a tale.
senses.whyCN: 线合成布，为细节合成为故事提供了意象。

senses.title: The pattern of a fabric
senses.definition: the way threads are crossed in a particular cloth, seen as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 某块布上线的交错方式，作名词
senses.example: The weave of the cloth is loose enough to let air through.
senses.exampleCN: 这块布织得够松，透得过气。
senses.why: The noun names the pattern that the verb produced.
senses.whyCN: 名词指动词所生产的那种纹样。

intro.en: Weave goes back to Old English wefan, a Germanic weaving word, and its irregular past wove and woven are the oldest forms.
intro.cn: weave 可上溯到古英语 wefan，是日耳曼语中的纺织词，不规则过去式 wove、woven 是最古老的形式。

items.en: The root is linked to an Indo-European word for weaving, seen also in Latin texere.
items.cn: 这一词根与印欧语中表示编织的词相连，也见于拉丁语 texere。

items.en: Wefan meant to weave, and the past forms wæf and wefen survive as wove and woven.
items.cn: wefan 意为编织，其过去式 wæf、wefen 留存为 wove、woven。

items.en: The verb kept its strong forms while gaining a weak weaved used for the winding sense.
items.cn: 动词保留了强变化形式，同时又长出弱变化 weaved，多用于蜿蜒义。

items.en: Weaving a story appears early, treating words as threads.
items.cn: 「编故事」很早就出现，把词语当作线。

items.en: Interweave and the textile noun weave spread the word into design.
items.cn: interweave 与纺织名词 weave 把这个词带入设计领域。

note.en: The first group shares the weave forms, the second the other verbs of making or winding.
note.cn: 第一组与 weave 同形同源，第二组是制作或蜿蜒的其他动词。

entries.definition: The ordinary past of weave.
Crossed threads turned into a finished cloth.
A person whose work is weaving.
To weave things into each other.
To make cloth from loops of yarn with needles.
To twist three or more strands together.
To follow a turning path.
To put parts together into a whole.

normalIntro.en: One crossing movement explains both the cloth and the winding road: something goes in and comes out again.
normalIntro.cn: 一个交错动作同时解释了布与蜿蜒的路：进去，再出来。

normal.en: Threads weave cloth; strips weave baskets.
normal.cn: 线织成布，条编成篮。

normal.en: The strong past is wove and woven; weaved suits winding paths.
normal.cn: 强变化过去式是 wove、woven；weaved 多用于迂回前行。

normal.en: A weaver is the person, weaving is the work.
normal.cn: weaver 是人，weaving 是活。

normal.en: Interweave means weave two things into one.
normal.cn: interweave 是把两样东西织在一起。

normal.en: Weaving a story treats words as thread.
normal.cn: weaving a story 把词语当作线。

abstract.en: Picture a shuttle sliding between tight threads.
abstract.cn: 想梭子在绷紧的线间滑过。

abstract.en: Hear the soft knock as each thread is pressed home.
abstract.cn: 听每根线被压紧时轻轻一响。

abstract.en: Watch cloth appear one line at a time.
abstract.cn: 看布一行一行出现。

examples.en: Villagers still weave baskets from local reeds.
examples.cn: 村民仍用本地芦苇编篮子。

examples.en: Our bus wove through the narrow streets.
examples.cn: 我们的车在窄巷里穿行。

examples.en: The cloth has a loose weave that keeps it cool.
examples.cn: 这种布织得较松，穿着凉爽。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威乌」——威乌太太手一推一拉，梭子在「威乌」声里来回，布就织成了。

root: 印欧语编织词根（见拉丁 texere）→ 古英语 wefan（编织）→ weave，wov、woven 为保留的强变化形式。

sensesIntro.en: The verb starts with threads crossing, extends to strips, then to paths and to stories, and the noun names the pattern made.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个动词从线交叉出发，扩展到长条、路径与故事，名词则指织出的纹样。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a shuttle crossing a warp.
core.cn: 核心意象：穿过经线的梭子。

branches.en: The cloth branch: wool woven into blankets.
branches.cn: 布匹分支：羊毛织成毯子。

branches.en: The craft branch: reeds woven into a basket.
branches.cn: 手艺分支：芦苇编成篮子。

branches.en: The path branch: a road weaving between hills.
branches.cn: 路径分支：山路蜿蜒。

branches.en: The story branch and the noun: tales woven and the weave counted.
branches.cn: 故事分支与名词：编故事与织法。

branches.en: The origin branch: wool crossed over and under.
branches.cn: 起源分支：上下交错的羊毛线。

intro.en: Weave takes native verb endings and the prefix inter-, and keeps an irregular past.
intro.cn: weave 采用本土动词词尾与前缀 inter-，并保留不规则过去式。

latinIntro.en: Latin texere is the true cousin behind the weave images, so the table gives its family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 texere 是编织意象背后的亲族，故拉丁表给出其同族词。

definition_en: in a way that breaks the law or the official rules
core_image: 一辆车斜停在消防通道上，轮胎压住了黄色禁停线
scene: 商场后门那条窄道本该空着，下午却被一辆车堵死。 Someone had parked illegally, blocking the exit for the delivery vans.
sceneCN: 这里 illegally 是「非法地、违法地」（第 1 个义项：以违反法律或规定的方式），句意是有人违章停车，把送货车的出口堵了。画面里有商场后门、黄线和斜停的车。

pos.zh: 副词：不法地、非法地、违法地

senses.title: In a way that breaks the law
senses.definition: by doing something that the law forbids
senses.definitionCN: 以做了法律禁止之事的方式
senses.example: The company illegally dumped waste into the river.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把废物非法倾倒入河。
senses.why: Adding -ly turns the adjective of legality into a description of how an action is carried out.
senses.whyCN: 加上 -ly 后，这个表示合法性的形容词转而描述一个动作是「怎么做出来的」。

senses.title: Against the rules of a game
senses.definition: in a manner that is not permitted by the rules of a sport
senses.definitionCN: 以体育规则不允许的方式
senses.example: He had moved the ball illegally with his hand.
senses.exampleCN: 他用手碰了球，属于犯规动作。
senses.why: Because the base word stretches to any code of rules, the adverb follows it onto the pitch.
senses.whyCN: 因为原形容词可以泛指一切规则，副词也跟着走上球场。

intro.en: Illegally is illegal plus the Old English adverb ending -lice, which in modern form is -ly.
intro.cn: illegally 是 illegal 加上古英语副词词尾 -lice，现代形式即 -ly。

items.en: Lex, law, was tied to legalis, and the negative phrase non legaliter described unlawful action.
items.cn: 拉丁语 lex（法律）派生出 legalis，而 non legaliter 之类说法已能形容违法行事。

items.en: French used the adverb illegalment for acting outside the law, showing the pattern was already productive.
items.cn: 法语用副词 illegalment 表示违法地做事，说明这一构词方式已很能产。

items.en: English adverbs were then made with -lice, the ancestor of -ly, attached to borrowed adjectives at will.
items.cn: 当时的英语副词由 -lice（-ly 的前身）构成，可以自由加在外来的形容词上。

items.en: Illegallie appeared in court writing, spelling the adverb with the -ly ending now usual.
items.cn: 法庭文书中出现 illegallie 的写法，副词以如今通行的 -ly 收尾。

items.en: Modern dictionaries settled the spelling as illegally, and the word spread to news reports of parking, dumping and smuggling.
items.cn: 现代词典把拼写定为 illegally，这个词也走进停车、倾倒、走私等新闻报道。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other -ly words whose base hides a negative prefix; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of wrongdoing.
note.cn: 形近组收其他以 -ly 结尾、词基里藏着否定前缀的词；近义组收表示做错事方式的副词。

entries.definition: In handwriting that cannot be read, sharing the shape but not the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 字迹难辨地；样子相近而意义无关。

entries.definition: In a way that does not follow reason, built with the same il- prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 不合逻辑地，前缀同样是 il-。

entries.definition: The same word without the negative prefix, meaning in a lawful way.
entries.definitionCN: 去掉否定前缀的同源副词，意为合法地。

entries.definition: In a way that is unjust or against the rules, often used of taking property.
entries.definitionCN: 不正当地、错误地，常用于取得财物。

entries.definition: In a manner not permitted by law; the closest plain synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 不合法地，最直白的同义说法。

entries.definition: In a hidden way; illegal acts are often also done in secret.
entries.definitionCN: 秘密地；违法行为常也偷偷进行。

normalIntro.en: The hooks tie the adverb ending to the question how, which is exactly what an adverb of manner answers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把副词词尾与「怎样」这个问题连起来，这正是方式副词所回答的。

normal.en: Take illegal and hang -ly on the end: the ending tells you it answers how.
normal.cn: 在 illegal 后面挂上 -ly：这个词尾说明它回答「怎样」。

normal.en: Two l's, then y, then the second word is an adverb: il-LEE-gal-ly.
normal.cn: 两个 l，再接 y：il-LEE-gal-ly，重音仍在第二拍。

normal.en: If the base word is an adjective of law, the -ly version describes the deed, not the person.
normal.cn: 如果原词是表示合法性的形容词，加 -ly 后描述的是行为而非人。

normal.en: Pair it with verbs of action: parked, dumped, imported, all take illegally naturally.
normal.cn: 与动作动词搭配最顺：parked、dumped、imported 都可自然接 illegally。

normal.en: Compare gently: legally is fine, illegally is not, and the only difference is the sound of a prefix.
normal.cn: 轻轻对比一下：legally 可以，illegally 不行，差别只在半秒的前缀音。

abstract.en: An adverb of this kind never names a person, only the shadow that a deed casts when the law looks at it.
abstract.cn: 这类副词从不点出人，只描出法律注视之下行为投出的那道影子。

abstract.en: The -ly ending is a lens: the crooked act stays the same, but the lens makes the crookedness visible.
abstract.cn: -ly 是一只镜片：歪的行为没变，是镜片让「歪」看得见。

abstract.en: Every rule needs a word for the way people slip past it, and this adverb is that word in miniature.
abstract.cn: 每条规则都需要一个词来描述人们绕过它的方式，这个副词就是那种词的小小化身。

examples.en: He was fined for parking illegally near the hospital gate.
examples.cn: 他因在医院门口违章停车被罚款。

examples.en: The timber was illegally cut from a protected forest.
examples.cn: 这批木材是从保护林里非法砍伐的。

examples.en: Anyone who acts illegally will be reported to the police.
examples.cn: 任何违法行事的人都会被举报给警方。

dict_mnemonic.text: illegal 非法的 + ly 副词尾——以违法的方式做某事

root: illegal（拉丁语 lex「法律」→ legalis，加否定前缀 in-→il-）加古英语副词词尾 -lice（今 -ly）。

sensesIntro.en: Two senses: acting against the law, and acting against the rules of a game.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项：违法行事，以及违反比赛规则地做动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a car angled across a yellow no-parking line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一辆车斜压在黄色禁停线上。

branches.en: THE STREET LINE: parking and dumping are the everyday crimes described this way.
branches.cn: 街头线：违章停车与乱倒废物是最日常的用法。

branches.en: THE FIELD LINE: a handball is an act done illegally on the pitch.
branches.cn: 球场线：手球就是球场上犯规地做的一个动作。

branches.en: THE COURT LINE: reports of illegal trading always use the adverb.
branches.cn: 法庭线：关于非法交易的报道总用这个副词。

branches.en: THE MANNER LINE: the ending answers how, never who.
branches.cn: 方式线：词尾回答「怎样」，从不回答「谁」。

branches.en: THE CONTRAST LINE: legally and illegally sit on opposite sides of one line.
branches.cn: 对照线：legally 与 illegally 分立在同一条线的两侧。

intro.en: Illegally is a three-part build: negative prefix, law root, and the native adverb ending.
intro.cn: illegally 是三段式构造：否定前缀、法律词根，以及本土的副词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The prefix and the root come from recorded Latin; the adverb ending is native English, not Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀与词根都来自有文献的拉丁语；副词词尾则是英语本土成分，并非拉丁语。

items.example: A legal adviser read the paper.
items.exampleCN: 一位法律顾问读了这份文件。

items.example: They fished illegally in the river.
Quietly and slowly both use it.
items.exampleCN: quietly 与 slowly 都用这个后缀。

items.example: They questioned the illegality of the tax.
items.exampleCN: 他们质疑这项税收的违法性。

items.meaning: in a way contrary to law

definition_en: a picture in a book, or an example used to make something clear
core_image: 翻开的旧书页上，一幅钢笔画正对着它解释的那段文字
scene: 孩子翻到动物百科讲章鱼的页面。 The illustration showed how the eight arms moved, and she read the text twice to compare.
sceneCN: 这里 illustration 是「插图、图解」（第 1 个义项：书中的图画），句意是插图展示了八条腕足如何活动，她把文字读了两遍来对照。画面里有翻开的书和钢笔画。

pos.zh: 名词：说明、图解、插图；例证

senses.title: A picture in a text
senses.definition: a drawing or photograph that appears in a book or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 出现在书籍或杂志中的图画或照片
senses.example: The manual has clear illustrations of each step.
senses.exampleCN: 这本手册为每个步骤都配了清晰的图示。
senses.why: The noun of the light verb naturally covers the picture whose job is to light up the text.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自「照亮」的动词，自然指承担照亮文字之责的那幅图。

senses.title: An example that explains
senses.definition: a case given in speech or writing to make a point clear
senses.definitionCN: 在口语或文字中用来讲清道理的事例
senses.example: His failure is an illustration of poor planning.
senses.exampleCN: 他的失败是计划不周的例证。
senses.why: Words can light things up as well as pictures, so the noun names an example used as a lamp.
senses.whyCN: 语言和图画一样能照亮事物，于是这个名词也指被拿来做灯的例子。

senses.title: The act of explaining or drawing
senses.definition: the work of explaining something or of drawing pictures for a publication
senses.definitionCN: 解释某事的工作，或为出版物作画的工作
senses.example: She earns a living from scientific illustration.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠科学插画为生。
senses.why: English often lets a -tion noun stand for the activity itself and for the trade built on it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常让 -tion 名词兼指活动本身与由此形成的行当。

intro.en: Illustration is the Latin noun of lighting up, carried into English through French.
intro.cn: illustration 是拉丁语中表示「照亮」的名词，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Illustratio meant a shedding of light, both literal and figurative.
items.cn: 拉丁语 illustratio 意为投射光明，既指实光也指比喻的光。

items.en: In learned prose the noun came to mean the act of making a matter plain by words.
items.cn: 在学术散文中，这个名词转指用言辞把问题讲明白。

items.en: French used illustration for a comment that illuminated a passage of text.
items.cn: 法语用 illustration 指照亮某段文字的注释。

items.en: English borrowed the word with a sense of distinction or enlightenment.
items.cn: 英语借入时，词义偏向「显赫」或「启迪」。

items.en: Printed books brought the modern sense, a picture placed beside words that explain them.
items.cn: 印刷书籍带来现代义：伴随解释文字的图画。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers -ation nouns from the same root; the near-meaning group gathers other words for pictures and examples.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词根的 -ation 名词；近义组收表示图画与例子的其他词。

entries.definition: The verb behind the noun, meaning to light up or add pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 名词背后的动词，意为照亮或配图。

entries.definition: Famous and bright with honour, from the same light family.
entries.definitionCN: 声名显赫的，同出光明一族。

entries.definition: Lighting, physical or mental; a near twin of this noun.
entries.definitionCN: 照明、启示，是本名词的近亲。

entries.definition: A line drawing that shows how parts are arranged.
entries.definitionCN: 用线条画出部件结构的图。

entries.definition: Any painted or printed image; the widest word of the group.
entries.definitionCN: 任何绘制或印刷的图像，范围最广。

entries.definition: A case used to show a rule; the verbal rival of sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 用来展示规则的实例，是第二个义项的口头对手。

normalIntro.en: The hooks join the -tion ending to the idea of a lamp beside a page of writing.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把 -tion 词尾与「文字旁边的一盏灯」这个意象连起来。

normal.en: Change the -ate of the verb to -ation and the action becomes a thing, a picture on the page.
normal.cn: 把动词的 -ate 换成 -ation，动作就变成了一样东西，即纸上的图。

normal.en: Stress the third syllable: il-lus-TRA-tion.
normal.cn: 重音落在第三音节：il-lus-TRA-tion。

normal.en: An illustration can be a picture or an example; both are lamps for a page.
normal.cn: illustration 可以是图也可以是例，两者都是照在纸页上的灯。

normal.en: -tion is the busiest noun ending in academic English, so it fits a word used in textbooks.
normal.cn: -tion 是学术英语里最忙的名词词尾，正配教材里的词。

normal.en: Children's books are judged by their illustrations before their words are read.
normal.cn: 童书常先看图再读字，这说明插图的位置。

abstract.en: The page carries a meaning and the picture carries a second one, and the reader meets them in the space between.
abstract.cn: 文字带一层意义，图画带另一层，读者在两者之间的空隙里相遇。

abstract.en: An example in an argument is a lamp placed where the reader stumbles.
abstract.cn: 论证中的例子，就是摆在读者绊脚处的灯。

abstract.en: The word keeps two trades alive at once: the scholar's comment and the artist's drawing.
abstract.cn: 这个词同时养着两门手艺：学者的注释与画家的画。

examples.en: The dictionary is full of small illustrations in the margin.
examples.cn: 这本词典的页边布满小插图。

examples.en: By way of illustration, consider two students with the same marks.
examples.cn: 举例来说，看看两位分数相同的学生。

examples.en: Her illustrations made the science book easy to follow.
examples.cn: 她的插图让这本科普书容易读懂。

dict_mnemonic.text: illustrate 配图、阐明 + ion 名词尾——插图；例证

root: 拉丁语 lustrare「照亮」→ illustratio「照明、阐明」，经古法语 illustration 进入英语，近代定指书中插图与例证。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a picture inside a text, an example that explains, and the work of illustrating.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：文字中的图画、用来解释的例子，以及绘图或解释这项工作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a black-ink drawing facing the paragraph it explains.
core.cn: 核心意象：一幅钢笔插图正对着它解释的那段文字。

branches.en: THE PAGE LINE: books, manuals and magazines place pictures among words.
branches.cn: 纸页线：书籍、手册与杂志把图放进文字里。

branches.en: THE ARGUMENT LINE: a failure or a case can stand as illustration.
branches.cn: 论证线：一次失败或一个案例就可充当例证。

branches.en: THE STUDIO LINE: scientific illustration is a paid craft.
branches.cn: 工作室线：科学插画是一门挣钱的手艺。

branches.en: THE ARTIST LINE: the illustrator's work ends up as an illustration.
branches.cn: 画家线：插图作者的工作最终落成一幅插图。

branches.en: THE EYE LINE: pictures speak to the eye, examples to the mind.
branches.cn: 眼睛线：图对眼睛说话，例子对头脑说话。

intro.en: Illustration is a Latin light root plus the noun ending -ion, with a rich family of related forms.
intro.cn: illustration 是拉丁语光之词根加名词词尾 -ion，周围有一整套同族形式。

latinIntro.en: Lustr- and the ending -io are both documented in Latin; the English -tion is their regular descendant.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 lustr- 与词尾 -io 在拉丁语中都有记录，英语的 -tion 是它们的规律继承者。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或结果的名词词尾
items.example: Action and creation follow the same pattern.
items.exampleCN: action 与 creation 遵循同样规律。

items.example: The illustration shows the whole engine.
items.exampleCN: 这幅插图展示了整台发动机。
这本图册收录了五十幅插图。

items.meaning: to add pictures or make clear
items.exampleCN: 他为自己的讲座画了插图。

items.example: It is an illustrative example, not a rule.
items.exampleCN: 这是个说明性的例子，不是规则。
这位插图作者用水彩作画。
一个显赫的家族曾住在这里。

definition_en: a person who sells food and small household goods
core_image: 街角小店的主人把纸袋递给顾客
scene: 街角的杂货商认得每位邻居。 The grocer on the corner knows every neighbour.
sceneCN: 这里 grocer 是「杂货商」（第 1 个义项）；句意：街角的杂货商认得每位邻居。

senses.title: Food shopkeeper
senses.definition: a person who sells food and small goods in a shop
senses.definitionCN: 在店里出售食品和小商品的人
senses.example: The grocer on the corner knows every neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 街角的杂货商认得每位邻居。
senses.why: This is the standard modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代标准义项。

senses.title: The shop itself
senses.definition: the shop where a grocer works, often called the grocer's
senses.definitionCN: 杂货商经营的店铺，常称 the grocer's
senses.example: We bought bread at the grocer's.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在杂货店买了面包。
senses.why: In British speech the shop takes the person's name.
senses.whyCN: 英式口语里，店铺直接用「商人的」来称呼。

senses.title: Old wholesaler
senses.definition: a merchant who sold goods in large amounts, an older sense
senses.definitionCN: 旧时成批出售货物的商人
senses.example: In old records the grocer sold goods by the barrel.
senses.exampleCN: 旧记录里，那位批发商按桶出售货物。
senses.why: The word first meant a wholesale dealer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初指批发商。

intro.en: Grocer comes from Old French grossier, a wholesaler, from Latin grossus, large or coarse.
intro.cn: grocer 来自古法语 grossier（批发商），源头是拉丁语 grossus（大的、粗的）。

items.en: Grossus meant large or coarse.
items.cn: grossus 意为大的、粗的。

items.en: Grossarius meant a wholesale dealer.
items.cn: grossarius 意为批发商。

items.en: Grossier meant a wholesaler.
items.cn: grossier 意为批发商。

items.en: Grocer meant a dealer in bulk goods.
items.cn: grocer 指大宗货物的经销商。

items.en: The sense narrowed to a food shopkeeper.
items.cn: 词义收窄为食品杂货商。

note.en: Grocer is compared with look-alike words and words for shopkeepers.
note.cn: 把 grocer 与形近词以及表示店主的词作比较。

normal.en: The grocer opened early.

abstract.en: Big trade began with small sacks.

abstract.en: The name of a trader can become the name of a shop.

sensesIntro.cn: grocer 指食品杂货商、杂货店，或旧义「批发商」。

core.en: A person who keeps and sells everyday food.
core.cn: 经营并出售日常食品的人。

branches.en: A shopkeeper weighs out sugar.
branches.cn: 店主称出一份糖。

branches.en: A bell rings as the door opens.
branches.cn: 门一开，铃就响了。

branches.en: Barrels wait in an old warehouse.
branches.cn: 旧仓库里堆着木桶。

branches.en: Shopkeeper and shop share one name.
branches.cn: 店主与店铺，共用一个称呼。

branches.en: Retail grew out of wholesale trade.
branches.cn: 零售从批发贸易中生长出来。

intro.en: Grocer forms plurals and a family of food-shop words.
intro.cn: grocer 构成复数以及一组与食品店相关的词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is grossus, large or coarse.
latinIntro.cn: 其拉丁语源头是 grossus，意为大的、粗的。

items.exampleCN: 好几家杂货商卖本地蜂蜜。

definition_en: a strong wish or urge to do something, especially something wrong or unwise
core_image: 一根挂在眼前的胡萝卜，越忍越香
scene: 减肥的人站在甜品店橱窗前，玻璃把香气都递了过来。 She resisted the temptation of the chocolate cake.
sceneCN: 这里 temptation 是「诱惑」（第 1 个义项：做不该做之事的强烈欲念）；句意：她抵挡住了巧克力蛋糕的诱惑。

derivatives.zh: 引诱；怂恿（动词原形，-ation 为名词后缀）
诱人的（现在分词转形容词）
诱惑者（动词加表人后缀）

senses.title: An urge to do something wrong or unwise
senses.definition: a strong wish to do something that one should not do
senses.definitionCN: 想做不该做之事的强烈愿望
senses.example: He could not resist the temptation to check his phone.
senses.exampleCN: 他忍不住想看手机。
senses.why: The image is bait: an outside pull that tests the will, as if something were dangled before you.
senses.whyCN: 意象是诱饵：一种试探意志的外来拉力，仿佛有什么东西在你眼前晃。

senses.title: Something that attracts strongly
senses.definition: a thing or person that makes someone want it
senses.definitionCN: 使人产生强烈欲望的事物或人
senses.example: The dessert tray was a temptation we could not refuse.
senses.exampleCN: 甜品托盘是我们无法拒绝的诱惑。
senses.why: The pull becomes a thing you can point at: the bait itself is named temptation.
senses.whyCN: 拉力被落成实物：诱饵本身就被叫作 temptation。

senses.title: A test of character in religious use
senses.definition: in religious language, a trial that tests faith or obedience
senses.definitionCN: 宗教语境中考验信仰或顺从的试炼
senses.example: The prayer asks to be led away from temptation.
senses.exampleCN: 祷文祈求远离试探。
senses.why: Here the bait is set deliberately, not by desire but by the tester, making the pull a trial.
senses.whyCN: 这里的诱饵是被刻意放置的：设局者并非欲望本身，试探成了考验。

intro.en: Temptation comes from Latin temptare or tentare, to test, try, or stretch toward, through Latin temptatio and Old French.
intro.cn: temptation 源自拉丁语 temptare/tentare「试探、尝试、向…伸去」，经 temptatio 与古法语传入英语。

items.en: Temptare meant to feel after, test, or try; some scholars link it with tendere, to stretch toward.
items.cn: temptare 意为试探、尝试；有学者将其与 tendere「朝…伸展」相联。

items.en: Temptatio named a trial or an attempt, later a testing of the soul.
items.cn: temptatio 指试炼或尝试，后指对灵魂的考验。

items.en: Old French temptacion carried the religious trial sense into medieval life.
items.cn: 古法语 temptacion 带着宗教试炼义进入中世纪生活。

items.en: English borrowed the word with both senses: testing and luring.
items.cn: 英语借入该词时兼有两义：考验与诱引。

items.en: The everyday lure sense prevailed; the trial sense survives mainly in religious language.
items.cn: 日常「诱引」义占了上风；「试炼」义主要存活于宗教语言。

note.en: Temptation is compared with its own verb family and with words for desire and pull.
note.cn: 把 temptation 与其动词词族，以及表示欲望与拉力的词对比。

entries.definition: to try to make someone do something
attractive, making you want it
to try; a try itself
entries.definitionCN: 尝试；企图，保留「试」的拉丁义

entries.definition: the quality of being powerfully attractive
a strong inner wish
a thing that attracts, like bait

normalIntro.en: Real links: temptare to test, attempt as a cousin, the bait image, and resist or give in.
normalIntro.cn: 真实联系：temptare「试探」、attempt 这个表亲、诱饵意象、resist 与 give in。

normal.en: Temptare means to test; every temptation tests your will.
normal.cn: temptare 意为试探；每次诱惑都在测你的意志。

normal.en: Attempt keeps the old test sense: an attempt is a try.
normal.cn: attempt 保留古义「试」：attempt 就是尝试。

normal.en: The carrot picture: temptation is a pull from outside.
normal.cn: 胡萝卜画面：诱惑是来自外面的拉力。

normal.en: Resist the temptation, or give in to it: two verbs of one tug-of-war.
normal.cn: resist 与 give in：同一场拔河的两个动词。

normal.en: Tempting food is bait shaped like dinner.
normal.cn: 诱人的食物就是做成晚餐形状的诱饵。

abstract.en: Every temptation is a small experiment on your will.
abstract.cn: 每次诱惑都是对你意志的小实验。

abstract.en: The bait smells sweetest exactly when the will is weakest.
abstract.cn: 意志最弱时，诱饵正香。

abstract.en: Desire speaks first; character answers later.
abstract.cn: 欲望先开口，品格后作答。

examples.en: The smell of fresh bread was too much temptation for him.
examples.cn: 新鲜面包的香气对他诱惑太大。

examples.en: Resist the temptation to reply in anger.
examples.cn: 抵制怒气回复的冲动。

examples.en: A free holiday offer is a temptation few can refuse.
examples.cn: 免费度假的提议很少有人能拒绝。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「탬ptation」——念作「疼劈-too-申」：疼也要劈开那块蛋糕，申手去拿 → temptation 诱惑

root: 拉丁语 temptare「试探、尝试」（一说与 tendere「伸展」相关）→ temptatio「试炼、诱引」→ 古法语 temptacion → 英语 temptation。

sensesIntro.en: From a trial of the soul to the everyday pull of cake, phone and bargain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从对灵魂的试炼，到蛋糕、手机与折扣的日常拉力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: bait dangled before the will.
core.cn: 核心意象：悬在意志面前的诱饵。

branches.en: The pull is felt, the bait unseen.
branches.cn: 拉力被感到，诱饵未被看见。

branches.en: The bait itself is named and priced.
branches.cn: 诱饵本身被点名标价。

branches.en: When the tester is divine, the trial is holy.
branches.cn: 当设局者是神，试炼便成圣课。

branches.en: Two verbs hang on it: resist and yield.
branches.cn: 两个动词挂在其上：抵制与屈服。

branches.en: Every urge is a test wearing a costume.
branches.cn: 每个冲动都是化了装的试验。

intro.en: Temptation belongs to the Latin temptare family with tempt, attempt and tempting.
intro.cn: temptation 属拉丁 temptare 词族，同族有 tempt、attempt、tempting。

latinIntro.en: Latin temptare, to test or try, possibly related to tendere, to stretch toward; the link is proposed, not certain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 temptare「试探」，可能与 tendere「朝…伸展」相关；此说未确证。

definition_en: something added to improve or complete another thing
core_image: 一杯水旁放着一片维生素，补足饮食的缺口
scene: 这种药片是维生素补充剂。 This tablet is a vitamin supplement.
