dict_mnemonic.text: supplement 是「补充物」，作动词表示补充；vitamin supplement 是维生素补充剂，supplementary 是补充的。注意与 complement（补全）区分。

root: 来自拉丁语 supplere（填满），由 sub（在下）与 plere（填满）组成，字面是「在下面填满」，引申为补充。

sensesIntro.en: Supplement means something added to complete a thing, the act of adding, or an extra publication section.
sensesIntro.cn: supplement 表示补全某物的添加物、补充的动作，或报刊的增刊。

core.en: An addition that fills a gap.
core.cn: 填补缺口的添加。

branches.en: This tablet is a vitamin supplement.
branches.cn: 这种药片是维生素补充剂。

branches.en: She supplements her income with evening work.
branches.cn: 她靠晚间工作补充收入。

branches.en: The newspaper printed a weekend supplement.
branches.cn: 报纸印了一份周末增刊。

branches.en: The thing added and the act of adding share a word.
branches.cn: 添加物与添加动作共用一个词。

branches.en: The course is a supplement to the main textbook.
branches.cn: 这门课是主教材的补充。

intro.en: Supplement builds supplementary and supplementation.
intro.cn: supplement 可构成 supplementary 和 supplementation。

latinIntro.en: The base is Latin plere, to fill, with sub under.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是拉丁语 plere（填满），加上 sub（在下）。

latinEntries.example: Supplere is the source of supplement.
latinEntries.exampleCN: supplere 是 supplement 的来源。
plere 也演变为英语的 complete。

definition_en: only just; almost not at all
core_image: 赛跑终点线上，选手累得几乎站不住脚
scene: 他跑完比赛，累得几乎站不住。 He could scarcely stand after the race.
sceneCN: 这里 scarcely 是「几乎不」（第 1 个义项）；句意：比赛结束后他几乎站不住。

senses.title: Almost not
senses.definition: only just; almost not at all
senses.definitionCN: 仅仅勉强；几乎完全不
senses.example: I could scarcely hear her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 我几乎听不见她的声音。
senses.why: The core sense is a very small degree, close to zero.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是程度极小，接近于零。

senses.title: Only just now
senses.definition: only a very short time before, often with when
senses.definitionCN: 就在很短时间之前，常与 when 连用
senses.example: We had scarcely sat down when the phone rang.
senses.exampleCN: 我们刚坐下电话就响了。
senses.why: A very small amount of time becomes just now.
senses.whyCN: 极少的时间量引申为「刚刚」。

senses.title: Certainly not
senses.definition: used to emphasize that something is not true or possible
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调某事不真实或不可能
senses.example: This is scarcely the moment for jokes.
senses.exampleCN: 这可不是开玩笑的时候。
senses.why: Almost not becomes a strong denial in emphasis.
senses.whyCN: 「几乎没有」在强调中变成强烈的否定。

intro.en: Scarcely is scarce plus -ly, from Latin excarpsus, plucked out.
intro.cn: scarcely 由 scarce 加 -ly 构成，scarce 源自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘出的）。

items.en: Excarpsus means plucked out.
items.cn: excarpsus 意为被摘出的。

items.en: Scars meant sparing or limited.
items.cn: scars 意为节省的、有限的。

items.en: Scarce described a short supply.
items.cn: scarce 描述供应不足。

items.en: Scarcely added the adverb ending to scarce.
items.cn: scarcely 由 scarce 加副词词尾构成。

items.en: Scarcely is common in formal and literary sentences.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scarcely 常见于正式和文学语句。

note.en: Scarcely is compared with similar forms and with other negative adverbs.
note.cn: 把 scarcely 与形近形式以及其他否定副词作比较。

entries.definition: not enough
in a frightening way
a state of shortage
almost not
only just
not often

normalIntro.en: Scarcely is scarce with -ly, meaning almost not.
normalIntro.cn: scarcely 是 scarce 加 -ly，意为几乎不。

normal.en: Scarcely adds ly to scarce, just as safely adds ly to safe.
normal.cn: scarcely 像 safely 一样，在形容词后加 ly。

normal.en: Scarcely believe means you can almost not believe it.
normal.cn: scarcely believe 意为几乎不敢相信。

normal.en: Scarcely when means one thing follows another at once.
normal.cn: scarcely when 表示一事紧接着另一事发生。

normal.en: Hardly and scarcely are close synonyms.
normal.cn: hardly 与 scarcely 是近义词。

normal.en: The word is common in formal writing.
normal.cn: 这个词常见于正式写作。

abstract.en: Scarcely is the shadow of a yes that almost became a no.
abstract.cn: scarcely 是几乎变成否定的那一点肯定。

abstract.en: A scarce supply leaves scarcely any choice.
abstract.cn: 稀缺的供应让人几乎没有选择。

abstract.en: The adverb measures the distance between something and nothing.
abstract.cn: 这个副词衡量有与无之间的距离。

examples.en: She scarcely had time to eat.
examples.cn: 她几乎没有时间吃饭。

examples.en: Scarcely had he left when it began to rain.
examples.cn: 他刚离开就开始下雨了。

examples.en: I can scarcely believe the news.
examples.cn: 我几乎不敢相信这个消息。

dict_mnemonic.text: scarce 是「稀缺的」，加 -ly 成副词 scarcely，程度少到「几乎没有」。

root: 由 scarce 加 -ly 构成，scarce 源自拉丁语 excarpsus（被摘出的），核心义「少到几乎不存在」。

sensesIntro.en: Scarcely means almost not, only just, or certainly not.
sensesIntro.cn: scarcely 意为几乎不、刚刚才，或决不。

core.en: A degree so small that it is almost nothing.
core.cn: 小到几乎等于零的程度。

branches.en: The core sense of almost not at all.
branches.cn: 几乎完全不的核心义。

branches.en: A tiny amount of time becomes just now.
branches.cn: 极少的时间量变成「刚刚」。

branches.en: Emphasis turns almost not into certainly not.
branches.cn: 强调把「几乎没有」变成「决不」。

branches.en: Barely enough and only just share the same limit.
branches.cn: 勉强够与刚刚才共享同一限度。

branches.en: Almost nothing can deny something outright.
branches.cn: 几乎没有可以变为断然否定。

intro.en: Scarcely belongs to the scarce family of shortage words.
intro.cn: scarcely 属于 scarce 的短缺词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin excerpere, to pick out, is the distant root.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 excerpere（挑出）是远源。

items.example: The scarceness of food was serious.
items.exampleCN: 食物稀少的情况很严重。

definition_zh: 市长；镇长；市政长官；（法国历史上的）宫相
definition_en: the elected head of a city or town government, and in some places a ceremonial civic title
core_image: 市政厅门前站着一个人，手里握着象征这座城市的钥匙
scene: 早晨的市政厅台阶上铺着红毯，工作人员把剪彩用的绸带拉直。 The mayor opened the new library on a rainy Tuesday morning.
sceneCN: 这里 mayor 是「市长」（第 1 个义项：城市政府的民选首脑）；句意为市长在一个下雨的周二上午为新图书馆揭幕。图中可辨识物件：市政厅台阶、红毯、剪彩绸带。

derivatives.zh: 由 mayor 加 -al 构成，义为「市长的；市长职务的」
由 mayor 加阴性后缀 -ess 构成，旧指女市长或市长夫人
由 mayoral 加 -ty 构成，义为「市长职位；市长任期」

senses.title: The elected head of a city government
senses.definition: the person elected to lead the government of a city or a large town
senses.definitionCN: 被选出来领导城市或大城镇政府的人
senses.example: The mayor opened the new library on a rainy Tuesday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 市长在一个下雨的周二上午为新图书馆揭幕。
senses.why: Latin maior meant greater, and the leading citizen of a town was named as the greater one among its people.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maior 意为「更大的」，城镇里领头的那位市民就被称作众人中「更大」的那一个。

senses.title: A ceremonial civic title in some cities
senses.definition: a title held by the civic head of certain cities, often with ceremonial duties rather than daily administration
senses.definitionCN: 某些城市市政首脑所持的头衔，常承担礼仪职责而非日常行政
senses.example: The Lord Mayor rode in the first carriage of the parade.
senses.exampleCN: 市长勋衔持有者乘坐游行队伍的第一辆马车。
senses.why: In cities with a long charter history, the old title survived as ceremony while a separate council ran the daily work.
senses.whyCN: 在宪章历史悠久的城市里，旧头衔作为礼仪保留下来，日常事务则由另一个议会机构处理。

senses.title: The head of a small town or borough
senses.definition: the head of a town council in a small town or borough
senses.definitionCN: 小城镇或自治市镇议会的负责人
senses.example: The mayor of the village still keeps a shop on the main street.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子的镇长还在大街上开着一家铺子。
senses.why: The same office scales down: a small town still needs one person to speak for it, and the title travels with the size of the place.
senses.whyCN: 同一个职位可以缩小规模：小镇也需要一个人代表它说话，头衔便随地方大小一起移动。

senses.title: The chief officer of a royal household in Frankish history
senses.definition: the highest official of the royal household in the Frankish kingdoms, later the real power behind the throne
senses.definitionCN: 法兰克诸王国宫廷中的最高官员，后来成为王位背后的实际掌权者
senses.example: In the Frankish kingdom, the mayor of the palace held more power than the king.
senses.exampleCN: 在法兰克王国，宫相掌握的权柄比国王更大。
senses.why: The Latin maior was used for the leading officer of a household, and that court title passed into French and then into English history writing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maior 曾用来指宫廷中为首的官员，这个宫廷头衔经法语进入英语的历史书写。

intro.en: Mayor is a Latin comparative that became a French office and then an English title, so its history runs from greater to the greater one in town.
intro.cn: mayor 是一个拉丁语比较级，先变成法语中的官职，再成为英语头衔，它的历史从「更大」走到「城里更大的那位」。

items.en: Magnus meant great, and its comparative maior meant greater, the form behind major and mayor alike.
items.cn: magnus 意为「大的」，它的比较级 maior 意为「更大的」，是 major 与 mayor 共同的来源。

items.en: Maior was used of a leading person, and in late Latin it could name the chief officer of a household.
items.cn: maior 曾用来指为首的人，在晚期拉丁语中也可指宫廷中的首席官员。

items.en: Old French maire named the head of a town, a usage that spread with French town charters.
items.cn: 古法语 maire 指城镇的首脑，这一用法随法国城市宪章一起传播。

items.en: English borrowed the title after the Norman period and spelled it mair, meire and mayor before settling on one form.
items.cn: 诺曼时期之后英语借入这个头衔，先后拼作 mair、meire、mayor，最后固定为一种写法。

items.en: Modern English uses mayor for elected city heads, keeps Lord Mayor as a ceremonial title, and derives mayoral and mayoralty from it.
items.cn: 现代英语用 mayor 指民选的城市首脑，保留 Lord Mayor 作礼仪头衔，并由此派生 mayoral 与 mayoralty。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin comparative maior; the near-meaning group gathers other names for civic office.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁语比较级 maior 走；近义组收其他表示市政官职的说法。

entries.definition: Relating to a mayor or to the office of mayor.
entries.definitionCN: 与市长或市长职务有关的。

entries.definition: The office or the term of a mayor.

entries.definitionCN: 规模或重要性更大的；也指军衔。

entries.definition: The French word for mayor, the direct source of the English title.
entries.definitionCN: 法语中「市长」一词，是英语这个头衔的直接来源。

entries.definition: The elected head of a state or province.

entries.definitionCN: 负责一个地区或部门的官员。

normalIntro.en: The word is Latin for greater turned into an office, and its family keeps the same comparative stem.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是把拉丁语「更大的」变成一个官职，同族词保留着同一个比较级词干。

normal.en: Latin maior is the comparative of magnus, so mayor began as a way of naming the greater man in a town.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 maior 是 magnus 的比较级，所以 mayor 起初是用来指城里「更大的那位」。

normal.en: Major and mayor come from the same Latin word, which is why they look so close.
normal.cn: major 与 mayor 出自同一个拉丁词，所以它们看起来那么像。

normal.en: The -al in mayoral turns the title into an adjective, and -ty in mayoralty turns it into an office.
normal.cn: mayoral 的 -al 把头衔变成形容词，mayoralty 的 -ty 把它变成职位。

normal.en: Lord Mayor keeps an old ceremonial title, showing that the office once carried more ritual weight.
normal.cn: Lord Mayor 保留着一个古老的礼仪头衔，说明这个职位曾经带着更重的仪式色彩。

normal.en: A deputy mayor or an acting mayor steps in when the elected head is away, which is the same office under another name.
normal.cn: deputy mayor 或 acting mayor 在民选首脑不在时代行职责，仍是同一个职位的不同名目。

abstract.en: Picture a town meeting where everyone points to one person and says that one is greater.
abstract.cn: 想象一场镇民大会，大家指向一个人说：那一位更重。

abstract.en: The word moved from a household to a city, but the shape of the title never changed.
abstract.cn: 这个词从宫廷走到城市，头衔的形状却一直没变。

abstract.en: Mayor and major differ by one letter and share one root, a reminder that office and importance come from the same idea.
abstract.cn: mayor 与 major 只差一个字母又同出一源，提醒人职位与重要性本是同一个念头。

examples.en: The mayor opened the new library on a rainy Tuesday morning.
examples.cn: 市长在一个下雨的周二上午为新图书馆揭幕。

examples.en: She ran for mayor and won by a narrow margin.
examples.cn: 她竞选市长，以微弱优势获胜。

examples.en: In the Frankish kingdom, the mayor of the palace held more power than the king.
examples.cn: 在法兰克王国，宫相掌握的权柄比国王更大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「妹儿」——站在市政厅门口的那位「妹儿」就是市长；记住 mayor 是市长。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）的比较级 maior（更大的）经古法语 maire 进入英语；同族词含 ma- 或 maj- 词干，多与「更大、更重要」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the greater one in a town; the senses split into the elected city head, the ceremonial title, the small-town version, and the historical court officer.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是城里「更大的那位」；义项分出民选的城市首脑、礼仪头衔、小镇版本，以及历史上的宫廷长官。

branches.cn: 市政厅台阶上被剪断的红绸带

branches.en: a small shop open beside the village hall
branches.cn: 村公所旁开着的一家小铺

branches.cn: 游行队伍最前面的马车

branches.en: a household officer standing behind a throne

branches.en: a key handed over in front of the council chamber
branches.cn: 在议事厅前交接的一把钥匙

intro.en: The word is a Latin comparative filtered through French, with one suffix for the adjective and one for the office.
intro.cn: 这个词是经法语过滤的拉丁语比较级，加一个后缀得到形容词，再加一个后缀得到职位名。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 水坝；拦河坝；阻拦之物；筑坝拦住
definition_en: a wall built across a river to hold back water, or to hold water or feeling back
core_image: 一道水泥墙把河拦腰截住，上游涨成一片湖
scene: 河水被一道水泥墙拦腰截住，上游涨成一片湖。 They built a dam across the valley.
sceneCN: 这里 dam 指「水坝」（第 1 个义项：横在河上挡水的墙）；句意是他们在山谷里修了一座水坝。

senses.title: A wall across water
senses.definition: a wall built across a river to hold back water
senses.definitionCN: 横在河上用来挡水的墙
senses.example: They built a dam across the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在山谷里修了一座水坝。
senses.why: Water is stopped by the one thing it cannot flow through.
senses.whyCN: 水唯一流不过去的东西，就能把它挡住。

senses.title: A barrier of any kind
senses.definition: something that blocks a flow, like a heap of fallen trees
senses.definitionCN: 堵住流动的东西，例如一堆倒下的树
senses.example: A dam of fallen trees blocked the stream.
senses.exampleCN: 倒下的树堆成一道坝，堵住了小溪。
senses.why: Once a wall stops water, any wall can borrow the name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有墙挡住了水，别的挡墙也能借用这个名字。

senses.title: To hold back
senses.definition: to stop water or a strong feeling from flowing out
senses.definitionCN: 阻止水或强烈情绪流出来
senses.example: She dammed up her tears until she got home.
senses.exampleCN: 她一直忍到回家才让眼泪流出来。
senses.why: Feelings can be held back the way a river is.
senses.whyCN: 情绪也能像河一样被拦在后面。

intro.en: Dam comes from Middle English, probably from Old Norse dammr or Middle Dutch dam, both naming a barrier that holds water.
intro.cn: dam 来自中古英语，可能出自古诺斯语 dammr 或中古荷兰语 dam，二者都指挡水的障碍。

items.en: Dammr named a barrier that held water back.
items.cn: dammr 指把水拦住的障碍。

items.en: Dam named a mound or wall closing a stream.
items.cn: dam 指堵住溪流的土堤或墙。

items.en: Dam entered English for a barrier across a river.
items.cn: dam 进入英语，指横在河上的障碍。

items.en: The verb dam meant to stop the water.
items.cn: 动词 dam 意为把水拦住。

items.en: Dam also covers blocked feelings and beaver works.
items.cn: dam 也用于被压抑的情绪和河狸筑的坝。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the short dam- sound, and the meaning group names other barriers against water.
note.cn: 形近组共享短促的 dam- 音，近义组列出其他挡水的障碍。

root: 来自中古英语，可能借自古诺斯语 dammr 或中古荷兰语 dam，本义是堵水的土堤或墙；先指拦河的坝，后引申为一切阻塞之物，以及压抑情绪的动作。

sensesIntro.en: From a wall in a river, to any heap that blocks a flow, to the act of holding something back.
sensesIntro.cn: 从河中的一道墙，到任何堵住流动的堆物，再到把东西拦在后面的动作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall standing across a river, with a lake behind it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一道横在河里的墙，墙后积成一片湖。

branches.en: The basic shape is a wall set across moving water.
branches.cn: 最基本的形状，是横在流水上的一道墙。

branches.en: Any heap that stops a stream can take the name.
branches.cn: 任何堵住溪流的堆物都能用这个名字。

branches.en: The verb moves the wall inside, where feelings are held.
branches.cn: 动词把这道墙搬进身体里，用来拦住情绪。

branches.en: Concrete and fallen trees do the same work.
branches.cn: 混凝土和倒下的树，干的是同一件事。

branches.en: Stopping water and stopping tears are one gesture.
branches.cn: 拦住水和拦住眼泪，是同一个动作。

intro.en: Dam is a short borrowing with a narrow family, all of it about holding water or feeling back.
intro.cn: dam 是个短小的借词，词族很窄，全都关于拦住水或情绪。

latinIntro.en: This word has no Latin root; it came from Old Norse or Middle Dutch.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，它来自古诺斯语或中古荷兰语。

items.meaning: a wall that holds back water

items.exampleCN: 被拦住的河水涨得很快。

items.meaning: the act of building a dam
items.example: Damming the stream killed the fish.
A beaver dam crossed the creek.
items.exampleCN: 一道河狸坝横在小溪上。

items.example: The hydroelectric dam lights the town.
items.exampleCN: 这座水电站大坝为镇上供电。

items.meaning: the place chosen for a dam

definition_en: to throw something away because it is no longer wanted
core_image: 楼道口一只旧沙发，坐垫裂开，露出里面的黄海绵
scene: 搬家的人把旧箱子一件件抬到楼下，堆在墙边。 They discarded the broken chairs behind the shop.
sceneCN: 这里 discarded 指「丢弃」（第 1 个义项：当作没用的东西扔掉）；句意是他们把坏椅子扔在店后面。

senses.title: To throw an object away
senses.definition: to get rid of something that is broken or no longer wanted
senses.definitionCN: 把坏掉或不再需要的东西处理掉
senses.example: They discarded the broken chairs behind the shop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把坏椅子扔在店后面。
senses.why: The hand lets go, and the object becomes someone else's problem.
senses.whyCN: 手一松，那件东西就成了别人的麻烦。

senses.title: To give up an idea or plan
senses.definition: to stop considering a plan or belief as useful
senses.definitionCN: 不再认为某个计划或想法有用
senses.example: The team discarded the first design.
senses.exampleCN: 团队放弃了第一版设计。
senses.why: An idea can be dropped as easily as a torn coat.
senses.whyCN: 一个想法，可以像破外套一样被丢下。

senses.title: To lay down a card
senses.definition: to put down a card that is no longer needed in a game
senses.definitionCN: 在牌局中打出不再需要的牌
senses.example: He discarded a low card and kept the ace.
senses.exampleCN: 他打出一张小牌，留下了爱司。
senses.why: What leaves the hand still lies on the table.
senses.whyCN: 离开手的东西，仍旧躺在桌上。

intro.en: Discard is dis-, away, plus card, a piece of stiff paper, and first meant to throw out a card.
intro.cn: discard 是 dis-（离开）加 card（硬纸片），最初指把牌打出去。

items.en: Charta meant paper or a written sheet.
items.cn: charta 指纸或写字的纸页。

items.en: Carta named a playing card in Italian games.
items.cn: carta 在意大利的牌戏里指一张牌。

items.en: Carte carried the same sense into French card games.
items.cn: carte 把同样的意思带进法国牌戏。

items.en: To discard was to throw a card out of the hand.
items.cn: discard 最初指把一张牌从手里打出去。

items.en: The verb widened to any object or idea thrown away.
items.cn: 这个词后来扩展到任何被扔掉的东西或想法。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the disc- opening, while the meaning group names other ways of letting things go.
note.cn: 形近组共用 disc 这一开头，近义组则列出其他放手的方式。

entries.definition: disagreement or a harsh mixture of sounds
entries.definitionCN: 不合，或刺耳的声音混杂

entries.definition: a style of dance music with a strong beat
entries.definitionCN: 节奏强烈的迪斯科舞曲

entries.definition: a heavy disc thrown in athletics
entries.definitionCN: 田径比赛中掷出的重圆盘

entries.definition: to get rid of something in a careless way
to leave something behind for good
entries.definitionCN: 把某物永久地留下不管

entries.definition: to cancel or throw out something useless
entries.definitionCN: 取消或扔掉无用的东西

normalIntro.en: These hooks move from a chair left by a wall to a card laid on a table.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从靠墙丢下的椅子，走到摊在桌上的一张牌。

normal.en: Dis- plus card: the card leaves the hand.
normal.cn: dis- 加 card：那张牌离开了手。

normal.en: Old chairs are discarded where nobody has to look.
normal.cn: 旧椅子总被丢在没人愿意看的地方。

normal.en: A plan can be discarded before it costs a penny.
normal.cn: 一个计划可以在花一分钱之前就被放弃。

normal.en: In a card game, discarding is a way of choosing.
normal.cn: 在牌局里，打出一张牌也是一种选择。

normal.en: What is discarded is not always worthless.
normal.cn: 被丢掉的东西，并不总是没有价值。

abstract.en: Picture a sofa with its cushion split open.
abstract.cn: 想象一只沙发的坐垫裂开了。

abstract.en: Picture a box left against a wall in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象一只箱子被丢在墙边淋雨。

abstract.en: Picture one card sliding face up across a table.
abstract.cn: 想象一张牌正面朝上滑过桌面。

examples.en: They discarded the broken chairs behind the shop.
examples.cn: 他们把坏椅子扔在店后面。

examples.en: The team discarded the first design.
examples.cn: 团队放弃了第一版设计。

examples.en: He discarded a low card and kept the ace.
examples.cn: 他打出一张小牌，留下了爱司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 discard 记成「的士卡的」：的士被卡在路上，乘客干脆丢下行李走了，就是丢弃。

root: 由表示「离开」的 dis- 加 card（纸牌）构成，字面就是「把牌打出去」。这个词先用于牌戏，指打出不要的牌；后来扩展到把旧物扔掉，再进一步指放弃想法、计划或习惯。

sensesIntro.en: From a broken chair left by a wall, to an idea dropped by a team, to a card laid on the table.
sensesIntro.cn: 从墙边丢下的坏椅子，到团队放弃的想法，再到摊在桌上的牌。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand opening and letting an object fall away.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手松开，让东西落下去。

chain: A HAND HOLDS AN OLD CHAIR

branches.en: The first sense is an object thrown away.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是被扔掉的实物。

branches.en: The second sense is an idea given up.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是被放弃的想法。

branches.en: The third sense is a card put down in a game.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是牌局里打出的一张牌。

branches.en: Things and plans both become lighter once dropped.
branches.cn: 东西和计划一旦丢下，都会变轻。

branches.en: A thrown chair and a played card both leave the hand.
branches.cn: 扔掉的椅子和打出的牌，都离开了手。

intro.en: Discard belongs to the card family, words about paper, maps and games.
intro.cn: discard 属于 card 一族，围绕纸片、图与牌戏。

latinIntro.en: Latin charta, paper, gives card and its relatives, including discard.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 charta（纸）给出 card 及其亲属词，包括 discard。

items.example: She wrote the address on a card.
items.exampleCN: 她把地址写在一张卡片上。

items.meaning: thick stiff paper used for boxes
items.example: The books came in a cardboard box.
The chart shows the rise in prices.
items.exampleCN: 图表显示了物价的上涨。

items.example: The city was founded by royal charter.
items.exampleCN: 这座城依王室特许状建立。

items.example: The cups are cheap and discardable.
items.exampleCN: 这些杯子便宜，用完就可扔。

items.example: A discarded tyre lay in the ditch.
items.exampleCN: 一条被丢弃的轮胎躺在沟里。
清理旧文件能省出空间。

definition_en: to invent or plan something by thinking carefully
core_image: 桌上摊着草图，铅笔在纸上改了又改
scene: 几个人围着白板，把方案擦了又写，一直弄到天亮。 They devised a plan to cut costs without losing staff.
sceneCN: 这里 devise 指「设计」（第 1 个义项：想出并安排出一个方案）；句意是他们设计出一个既降成本又不裁员的方案。

senses.title: Invent a plan
senses.definition: to invent a plan or method by thinking carefully
senses.definitionCN: 经过仔细思考发明出一个方案或方法
senses.example: They devised a plan to cut costs without losing staff.
senses.exampleCN: 他们设计出一个既降成本又不裁员的方案。
senses.why: A plan does not exist until someone draws its first line.
senses.whyCN: 在有人画出第一道线之前，方案并不存在。

senses.title: Think up a clever way
senses.definition: to find a clever way of doing something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 为做成一件难事找出一个巧妙的办法
senses.example: She devised a trick to open the locked door.
senses.exampleCN: 她想出一个打开锁门的巧办法。
senses.why: The obstacle stays the same; the new path is the invention.
senses.whyCN: 障碍没有变，被发明出来的是那条新路。

senses.title: Arrange a formal system
senses.definition: to create and arrange a formal system, rule or document
senses.definitionCN: 制定并安排好一套正式的制度、规则或文件
senses.example: The committee devised new rules for the contest.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会为比赛拟订了新规则。
senses.why: Rules are a machine made of sentences, and someone must build it.
senses.whyCN: 规则是用句子做成的机器，总得有人把它造出来。

intro.en: Devise comes from Old French deviser, to arrange or talk over, which grew from Latin dividere, to divide, and it shares a root with device.
intro.cn: devise 来自古法语 deviser（安排、商议），源头是拉丁语 dividere（分开），与 device 同源。

items.en: Dividere meant to divide a whole into parts.
items.cn: dividere 指把一个整体分成几部分。

items.en: Deviser meant to arrange, discuss or plan something in parts.
items.cn: deviser 指把事情分块安排、商议或计划。

items.en: English devise first meant to plan or to bequeath property.
items.cn: 英语 devise 最初指筹划，也指遗赠财产。

items.en: The planning sense grew stronger and the legal sense faded.
items.cn: 计划这一层越来越强，法律遗赠那层渐渐淡出。

items.en: It now means to invent a method, a system or a clever answer.
items.cn: 如今它指发明一种方法、一套制度或一个巧妙的答案。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the vis sound, while the meaning group moves from inventing to contriving and drafting.
note.cn: 形近组共用 vis 这一段音，近义组则从发明走到设法与拟订。

entries.definition: a machine made for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 为某种用途制造的机器

entries.definition: indirect or not honest
a suggestion about what to do
to create something that did not exist
entries.definitionCN: 造出原本不存在的东西

entries.definition: to manage to do something by clever planning
entries.definitionCN: 靠巧妙的安排设法做到

entries.definition: to express an idea in a clear plan
entries.definitionCN: 把想法写成清晰的方案

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a whiteboard covered in crossed-out lines and end with a page of new rules.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从写满涂改线的白板开始，落到一页新规则。

normal.en: Device is the thing; devise is the act of planning it.
normal.cn: device 是那个东西，devise 是把它计划出来的动作。

normal.en: The ending decides: a hiss for the noun, a buzz for the verb.
normal.cn: 词尾定词性：名词收清音，动词收浊音。

normal.en: To devise is to divide a hard job into small steps.
normal.cn: devise 就是把一件难活切成小步。

normal.en: A locked door invites a devised trick.
normal.cn: 一扇锁着的门，正好邀请一个想出来的巧办法。

normal.en: Rules are sentences arranged until they work.
normal.cn: 规则就是被排到能用的句子。

abstract.en: Picture a hand erasing half a line on a whiteboard.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手擦掉白板上半条线。

abstract.en: Picture three cups on a table and a coin underneath.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上三只杯子，其中一只下面压着硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a page of numbered rules with one blank line.
abstract.cn: 想象一页编号的规则，其中留着一行空白。

examples.en: They devised a plan to cut costs without losing staff.
examples.cn: 他们设计出一个既降成本又不裁员的方案。

examples.en: She devised a trick to open the locked door.
examples.cn: 她想出一个打开锁门的巧办法。

examples.en: The committee devised new rules for the contest.
examples.cn: 委员会为比赛拟订了新规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 devise 记成「地歪兹」：de 是分开，vis 是看，把难题拆开来看，就能设计出办法。

root: 来自古法语 deviser（安排、商议），源头是拉丁语 dividere（分开），与 device 同源。本义是把事情分块安排、筹划，后来法律上的遗赠义淡出，主要表示设计方法、想出办法与拟订制度。

sensesIntro.en: From drawing a first line of a plan, to finding a clever way past an obstacle, to writing rules that work.
sensesIntro.cn: 从画下方案的第一道线，到为障碍找一条巧路，再到写出能用的规则。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pencil crossing out a line and drawing it again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一支铅笔划掉一条线，又重新画一条。

branches.en: The first sense is the sketch becoming a plan.
branches.cn: 第一个义项是草图变成一个方案。

branches.en: The second sense is the clever turn that gets past a wall.
branches.cn: 第二个义项是绕过一堵墙的那个巧劲。

branches.en: The third sense is the plan written as rules.
branches.cn: 第三个义项是写成规则的方案。

branches.en: A plan and a trick are both shapes drawn by thought.
branches.cn: 方案与巧计，都是思考画出来的形状。

branches.en: A private sketch becomes a public system through words.
branches.cn: 私下的草图，靠文字变成公共的制度。

intro.en: Devise shares a family with device, and both grow from the idea of dividing and arranging.
intro.cn: devise 与 device 同属一族，二者都从「分开、安排」这个意思长出来。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base dividere means to divide, and the French verb added the sense of planning.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 dividere 意为分开，法语动词又添上计划的意思。

items.example: They devise new games each year.
items.exampleCN: 他们每年都设计新游戏。
这个测试是精心设计的。
这样的方案是设计得出来的。

items.example: The device fits in one hand.

items.exampleCN: 这些装置共用一个充电器。
这条路弯弯绕绕地往上去。

definition_zh: 爬行；悄悄移动；蔓延；（时间）悄然过去
definition_en: to move slowly and quietly, close to the ground or out of notice
core_image: 一个人贴着墙根慢慢挪动，尽量不发出声音
scene: 走廊里有人贴着墙根挪动，脚步几乎没有声音。 She tried to creep past the sleeping guard.
sceneCN: 这里 creep 指「悄悄移动」（第 1 个义项：贴着地面或墙根缓慢而不出声地移动）；句意是她想悄悄从睡着的门卫身边过去。

senses.title: Move low and quiet
senses.definition: to move slowly and quietly so as not to be noticed
senses.definitionCN: 缓慢而安静地移动，以免被察觉
senses.example: We crept up the stairs in the dark.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在黑暗里悄悄爬上楼梯。
senses.why: A body kept low makes less noise and less shadow.
senses.whyCN: 身体压低，声音更小，影子也更少。

senses.title: Spread over a surface
senses.definition: to spread slowly over a surface or through a place
senses.definitionCN: 沿着表面或在一个地方缓慢铺开
senses.example: Ivy creeps over the old stone wall.
senses.exampleCN: 常春藤在旧石墙上蔓延。
senses.why: Plants also travel an inch at a time, without legs.
senses.whyCN: 植物没有腿，也是一寸一寸地走。

senses.title: Of time, to slip by
senses.definition: of time, to pass so slowly and quietly that it is hardly felt
senses.definitionCN: 指时间缓慢而安静地过去，几乎察觉不到
senses.example: The afternoon crept by without a sound.
senses.exampleCN: 那个下午无声无息地溜走了。
senses.why: Slow hours move like a body trying not to be heard.
senses.whyCN: 缓慢的时辰像一具不愿被听见的身体在挪动。

intro.en: Creep comes from Old English creopan, to move on the belly or on hands and knees.
intro.cn: creep 源自古英语 creopan，指用腹部或手脚贴地移动。

items.en: Creopan meant to move on the belly or on hands and knees.
items.cn: creopan 指以腹部或手脚贴地移动。

items.en: It described animals and people alike.
items.cn: 它既用于动物，也用于人。

items.en: Crepen kept the same slow and low sense.
items.cn: crepen 保留了同样缓慢低伏的意思。

items.en: It gained the sense of moving without being seen.
items.cn: 它多了不被人看见地移动这一层意思。

items.en: It was used for plants spreading over walls.
items.cn: 它被用来形容植物在墙上蔓延。

items.en: Time too can creep past us.
items.cn: 时间也会从我们身边悄悄溜过。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the creep spelling, and the meaning group names other quiet ways of moving.
note.cn: 形近组保留 creep 这一串拼写，近义组列出其他安静的移动方式。

entries.definition: a plant that spreads along a wall
causing a feeling of fear
moved slowly and quietly
to move on hands and knees
to move in a way meant to escape notice
entries.definitionCN: 以不让人注意的方式移动

entries.definition: to walk on the toes to stay silent

normalIntro.en: These hooks start with a low body and end with a vine on a wall.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子从一具压低的身体开始，最后落到墙上的一根藤。

normal.en: Creep contains eep, a sound you never want to make.
normal.cn: creep 里有 eep，那正是你不想发出的声音。

normal.en: Lower the body, slow the feet, hold the breath.
normal.cn: 蹲低身体，放慢脚步，屏住呼吸。

normal.en: A cat on a fence at midnight knows how to creep.
normal.cn: 半夜蹲在篱笆上的猫，最懂怎么悄悄挪动。

normal.en: Vines creep because they cannot walk.
normal.cn: 藤只会蔓延，因为它不会走路。

normal.en: When the clock seems still, the hours creep.
normal.cn: 钟看着不动时，时辰其实在悄悄走。

abstract.en: Picture a shadow that moves while nobody looks.
abstract.cn: 想象一个趁人没看就移动的影子。

abstract.en: Picture a stem inching across a brick.
abstract.cn: 想象一根茎在砖面上慢慢蹭过去。

abstract.en: Picture a minute hand that refuses to hurry.
abstract.cn: 想象一根不肯快走的分针。

examples.en: The cat crept toward the bird.
examples.cn: 猫悄悄朝那只鸟靠近。

examples.en: A vine creeps up the garden wall.
examples.cn: 一根藤沿着花园的墙往上爬。

examples.en: A strange feeling crept over me.
examples.cn: 一种奇怪的感觉悄悄爬遍我全身。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 creep 记成一只猫压低身体往前走：脚步无声，一寸一寸地挪，就是悄悄移动。

root: 源自古英语 creopan（贴地爬行）；本义是以腹部或四肢贴地移动，引申为悄无声息地挪动、植物蔓延，以及时间悄然过去。

sensesIntro.en: From a body moving low and slow, to vines spreading and hours slipping away.
sensesIntro.cn: 从身体贴地慢行，到藤蔓蔓延、时光溜走。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a low body sliding along a wall in the dark.
core.cn: 核心意象：黑暗里一具压低的身体沿墙滑行。

branches.en: A person or animal moves low to avoid being heard.
branches.cn: 人或动物压低身体移动，以免被听见。

branches.en: Plants spread the same way, an inch at a time.
branches.cn: 植物也这样铺开，一次只挪一寸。

branches.en: Slow hours pass as quietly as a careful footstep.
branches.cn: 缓慢的时辰像小心的脚步一样安静地过去。

branches.en: Both a thief and a dull afternoon move without a sound.

intro.en: Creep is a native English verb whose family grows with -er, -y and -ing.

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the word is purely Germanic.
